Dems express ‘points of anxiety’ over Trump’s summit with Putin and Xi

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1205 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • President Donald Trump prepares to shake hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China's President Xi Jinping looks on before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, Nov.
  • Some Senate Democrats have heartburn about President Donald Trump’s planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, but Republicans counter by saying he could get the Russian and Chinese leaders to budge on a list of problems even as he appears politically weakened at home.
  • Recent findings suggest that trump arrived Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen economic zone on the banks of the Pearl River ahead of a high-level summit that was ostensibly slated to focus on paring each countries’ nuclear arsenal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

President Donald Trump prepares to shake hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China's President Xi Jinping looks on before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. (Iori Sagisawa / POOL / AFP via Getty Images).

Some Senate Democrats have heartburn about President Donald Trump’s planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, but Republicans counter by saying he could get the Russian and Chinese leaders to budge on a list of problems even as he appears politically weakened at home.

Recent findings suggest that trump arrived Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen economic zone on the banks of the Pearl River ahead of a high-level summit that was ostensibly slated to focus on paring each countries’ nuclear arsenal. But before he left, Trump signaled the three-way talks also likely would include the artificial intelligence race, Moscow’s bloody war with Ukraine, global trade and his standoff with Iran.

According to recent reports, the U.S. commander in chief’s tendency to sound deferential to Putin and habit of referring to Xi as a personal “friend” concerns many congressional Democrats. But Trump’s GOP allies on Capitol Hill, despite this month’s midterm election losses, still describe him as a dealmaker who has a chance to use his final years to bend Putin and Xi toward U.S. interests.

Rick Scott, a Florida Republican who sits on the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, said Tuesday he was hopeful that Trump could make some progress on at least one issue with the Russian and Chinese leaders.

“As we all know, China and Russia want to destroy our way of life,” he stated. “But it would be great to reduce … nuclear stockpiles and make sure we're not going to ever get attacked.

Still, Scott sounded skeptical about two world leaders Trump has tried to keep close during his two terms. “But do I trust Xi or Putin? No, they're a bunch of liars.” Asked if he worries Trump might trust them too much, Scott replied: “I don't think he trusts him any more than I do. … I'm glad the president's trying. Hope springs eternal. But do I actually really believe something good's going to come out of it? I don't.”.

Outgoing House Armed Services Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., said part of Trump’s talks on Thursday “should be to make sure the world is a safer place, to make sure we don't have aggressive behavior like Russia in an unprovoked attack against Ukraine.

“They ought to be talking about how they don't do those sorts of things, how they don't threaten their neighbors, how they don't try to intimidate through the assertion of force that they ought to be able to work together to make sure we assure a safe globe,” stated Wittman, who lost his reelection race earlier this month.

That comment came one day after Trump told reporters as he left the White House for Asia that he sees Putin “backing down a little bit” in his conduct of the war with Ukraine.

Industry observers note that “I think he could be tougher. I think he could be a lot tougher, frankly,” Trump noted Monday. “I think he's backing down.”.

Those kinds of deferential remarks about the Russian leader are a significant reason why some Democrats have heartburn about Thursday’s meeting.

Industry observers note that senate Armed Services member Mazie K. Hirono, D-Hawaii, noted Tuesday that she’s concerned about the Shenzhen summit because “I’m not sure what’s going to pop out of [Trump’s] mouth next — especially for a meeting with two guys he clearly likes.”.

According to recent reports, sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., also a member of the Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, mentioned he has “high hopes” for the trilateral meeting — but “maybe not high expectations.”.

“I have some points of anxiety. I'm nervous about any discussion about Ukraine that doesn't involve the Ukrainians. And, so, some of the advance to this is like, ‘We're going to talk about ending the Ukraine war.’ You can't do that without Ukraine at the table,” Kaine mentioned. “So the desire to bring about more peace and stability, that's a good thing to talk about. But no conditions about Ukraine and ending that war without them at the table? Not so sure about that.”.

During remarks Tuesday on the Senate floor, Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer criticized what he described as Trump’s misplaced priorities.

“Enforcement of the fresh rules restricting China’s access to our most sensitive AI chips should start today,” the New York Democrat said, adding that Trump should focus more of his Asia swing on securing commitments from U.S. allies to block China from gaining an upper hand in the AI technology race.

Trump touted just that on Tuesday during remarks in Manila at a U.S.-Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in the Philippines.

Recent findings suggest that “Since I returned to office, we've made major trade deals with Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia, as well as Japan, South Korea, and almost everybody, frankly, at the table,” he mentioned. “And we've made many other vital agreements across the region spanning energy, critical minerals and technology.”.

But on Wednesday, Trump appeared to have pivoted to the trip’s main event.

He stood beside Xi at an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen and smiled as Putin approached. Trump extended his hand and shook Putin’s as the Chinese leader looked on.

Scott, a Trump ally in the Senate, noted Tuesday he sees the president “trying to build relationships to try to make sure we don't end up at war [because] he doesn't like war.”.

Trump signaled Monday that he might press Xi for details on an alleged Chinese spy who had an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, costing the AI mogul his job as the company’s president and CEO. He also mentioned he could bring up Nvidia’s sales of sophisticated microchips that many lawmakers — Republican and Democrat — want to ensure remain in the U.S. for domestic AI development.

Industry observers note that the administration’s response to the turmoil at Nvidia, with Trump even suggesting he'd support Huang returning as CEO, is a rare area where Republicans have expressed concern publicly. House Energy and Commerce Committee Chair Brett Guthrie, R-Kent., wrote to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Wednesday seeking information about “the implementation of federal laws governing technology exports, in particular the application of export controls relating to semiconductor chips, the effect of which has a broad impact on America’s race with China to artificial intelligence (AI) dominance and the ability of U.S. companies to set global technology standards.”.

Heather Williams, director of the Project on Nuclear Issues at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, wrote this week that for the three leaders, the “path is fraught with challenges.”.

“Putin could diplomatically outmaneuver the Trump administration and make any progress on nuclear complications dependent on undermining Western support to Ukraine,” she wrote in an analysis for the Washington, D.C.-based think tank. “Even the optics of Trump and Putin negotiating while the war continues and as Russia ramps up missile strikes on Ukrainian civilian targets could be interpreted as undermining U.S. values.”.

How Many Miles Per Gallon Does A Boeing 747 Get?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1524 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, with its four engines, the Boeing 747 uses vast quantities of fuel, burning through 3,800 gallons every hour.
  • Recent findings suggest that we will also delve into ongoing debates around sustainable aviation fuel to explore if aviation can be sustainable.
  • According to the BBC's Future Planet, a cruising 747 burns through 0.9 gallons (four liters) of fuel each second.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, with its four engines, the Boeing 747 uses vast quantities of fuel, burning through 3,800 gallons every hour. This high fuel burn amounts to 0.9 gallons used every second and 0.19 miles per gallon (mpg). In this article, we will detail the Boeing 747's mpg further, including the mpg per traveler, and how this compares to travel in a car and in modern airliners.

Recent findings suggest that we will also delve into ongoing debates around sustainable aviation fuel to explore if aviation can be sustainable. After all, all airliners burn through staggering quantities of fuel.

According to the BBC's Future Planet, a cruising 747 burns through 0.9 gallons (four liters) of fuel each second. This is equivalent to 3,500 gallons (13,250 liters) of fuel every hour. If a 747 is cruising at its standard cruising speed of around 580 mph (933 km/h), it is covering a mile every 6.2 seconds.

In a recent development, covering a mile requires 5.9 gallons of fuel. As a result, a cruising Boeing 747 can achieve just 0.18 miles per gallon. However, this is not the full picture, as a 747 carries far more people than most aircraft. For example, Qantas' 747-400s carried 364 passengers across three classes.

Recent findings suggest that if we extrapolate this number of seats into the mpg that each passenger has, the data highlights 65.5 mpg per passenger. According to calculatormpg.co.uk, the baseline for a good car mpg is 50. If a car is carrying two people, then the car is achieving 100 passenger miles per gallon.

Industry observers note that this suggests that flying on a 747 still uses substantially more fuel than a car carrying multiple people, but less than a car carrying one person. The other difference to consider when comparing fuel consumption across modes of transport is that a 747 has to take off, which is not a concern for a car or train.

In a recent development, takeoff is the most fuel-intensive part of any flight as the jet has to get up to speed while it is at its heaviest, and then climb to cruising altitude. The exact fuel consumption during takeoff depends hugely on how close the aircraft is to its maximum takeoff weight (almost a million pounds). However, the general quantity of fuel needed is approximately 5,000 gallons (19,000 liters).

This consumption of fuel equates to a fuel burn of approximately 154,000 lbs (70,000 kg) for a flight from London to New York. To sustain such a high consumption, a 747 can carry a vast amount of fuel. The debut 747 could carry 48,400 gallons (183,000 liters) of fuel. Later variants increased this capacity to 63,034 gallons (238,610 liters) for the 747-8.

In a recent development, this vast ocean of fuel is stored primarily in the aircraft's wings. A 747 has two main fuel tanks in each wing, with further reserve fuel tanks in the wings' outer sections and central wing tanks. It is common for airliners to store fuel in the wings to free up fuselage space for cargo storage.

In a recent development, the primary fuel tanks are usually filled first. Any further fuel needed for the flight is put into the central wing tank. Any final drops needed are pumped into the reserve tanks. Select 747 models can increase fuel capacity further by sealing off part of the horizontal stabilizer and using it as an additional auxiliary tank.

In recent years, the 747-400F's fuel storage has come under FAA scrutiny due to improperly applied cap seals on some aircraft. Should these seals fail during a lightning strike or short circuit, it could allow arcing within the fuel tanks and cause an explosion.

Industry observers note that the FAA's attention came following several fuel tank explosions on commercial aircraft in the late 1990s. This led to a 2001 review titled ‘Transport Airplane Fuel Tank System Design Review, Flammability Reduction, and Maintenance and Inspection Requirements.’.

It has been revealed that the document led to a range of safety recommendations, including those relating to cap seals. In June 2022, the FAA responded to reports that cap seals were not being applied properly during production of the 747-400F. A design change omitted the application of the cap seals on eight fasteners, distributed equally across both wings.

It has been revealed that at a surface level, the similar MPG per traveler between a 747 and a modern car would suggest a similar amount of environmental harm. Moreover, the US Energy Information Administration claims that jet fuel produces 21.1 lbs of CO2 per gallon, which is comparable to the 19.6 lbs of greenhouse gas produced from burning a gallon of gasoline.

It has been revealed that however, focusing on CO2 alone hides the unique environmental harm caused by burning aviation fuel at altitude. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change points to the effects of water vapor clouds that contain black carbon, nitrous oxide, and sulfur dioxide.

Climate scientists use 'radiative forcing' as their measure for how environmentally harmful an activity is. A 2010 study by the University of Oslo’s International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis compared the radiative forcing of car and aircraft travel. The scientists concluded:.

In a recent development, "Air travel results in a lower temperature change per passenger-kilometer than car travel on the long run; the integrated radiative forcing of air travel is on short- to medium time horizons much higher than for car travel. Per passenger-hour traveled however, aviation’s climate impact is a factor 6 to 47 higher than the impact from car travel.".

It has been revealed that one reason the 747 burns so much fuel and has a poor mpg, causing greater environmental harm, is that it's an outdated airframe. This aircraft was first introduced in 1970, and the technology available 56 years ago was substantially less advanced than aircraft technology today.

Sources indicate that as a result, the 747 would be considered incredibly inefficient if it were produced today. Furthermore, modern airliners are far lighter than the 747, needing less fuel for takeoff. 21st-century widebody, and notably two-engine, aircraft are far more efficient due to modern technology.

Industry observers note that they burn less fuel. However, because they carry fewer passengers than the behemoth 747, they don't necessarily have a better mpg per passenger. The Airbus A350 was introduced in 2015 with Qatar Airways, becoming the first Airbus aircraft constructed primarily with carbon-fibre-reinforced polymers.

In a recent development, simple Flying reported that this aircraft burns 2,700 gallons per hour, or 0.75 gallons per second. With a cruising speed of 561 mph, the aircraft travels a mile every 6.4 seconds and has a cruising mpg of 0.208. Qantas's upcoming A350-1000s will have 238 seats across four classes, yielding an mpg per passenger of 50. This is equivalent to a modern car with only the driver on board.

It has been revealed that A Boeing 787 Dreamliner has also advanced the field of environmentally conscious aviation. The Dreamliner was first introduced in October 2011 with All Nippon Airways. This jetliner burns 2,900 gallons of fuel per hour, and its cruising speed is 561 mph. As a result, the aircraft burns 5.17 gallons per mile, yielding an mpg of 0.193. Meanwhile, a Qantas 787-9 Dreamliner has 236 seats across three classes, so each passenger gets 44.8 mpg during the cruise.

We can see that even modern airliners consume vast quantities of fuel, causing significant environmental harm. Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) could be a pathway to mitigate the harm of this enormous fuel consumption. SAF is defined as aviation fuel that is not derived from fossil fuels, but has near-identical performance characteristics.

It can be mixed with conventional fuel, and aircraft don't have to be re-engineered. Its development has come with a host of benefits and challenges. IATA's criteria for fuel to be considered sustainable are that it must reduce CO2 emissions across its lifecycle, not require excess freshwater, not compete with food production, and not cause deforestation.

If SAF can be rolled out, it could transform the aviation sector's sustainability. A ScienceDirect study based on the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation found that SAF could allow greenhouse gas emissions to decrease by up to 94%. Airbus puts this number closer to 80%.

According to recent reports, SAF has begun to be seen in action within the commercial aviation sector. Virgin Atlantic operated the first 100% SAF flight in 2023, flying a Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner with Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 engines. Rolls-Royce has since claimed to be the only engine manufacturer to confirm that all its powerplants work with SAF.

However, SAF rollout has not yet been substantial, primarily due to economic challenges: SAF costs an average of $6 per gallon, while fossil-fuel-based jet fuel typically costs $2.29 per gallon (although it has been on the rise amid the Iran War). The high cost is primarily due to low production rates, as just 33 million gallons of SAF were produced in the US in 2021. The US Department of Energy estimated in 2022 that SAF production would have to increase to 3 billion gallons annually.

The concept of mileage running is making headlines in Japan, and not in a good way. A lucrative promotion from Japan Airlines reportedly caused passengers to take up to 12 flights per day in remote markets, in some cases making it difficult for locals to book flights. What a story this is!

News On Japan has the story of how mileage running has caused complications for locals on some of Okinawa’s remote islands, as they’ve struggled to purchase Japan Airlines tickets due to a flood of mileage runners.

Sources indicate that while the story has been published in recent days, it seems to date back to February 2026 (best I can tell), when Japan Airlines’ Mileage Bank program was offering double Life Status Points for flights. This promotion incentivized all domestic flights equally, so some savvy frequent flyers decided to seek out the shortest flights, so that they could cram in as many flights in a day as possible.

This ended up bringing them to Okinawa, where you’ll find some of the shortest flights in Japan Airlines’ system. These include flights between Ishigaki (ISG), Miyako (MMY), Naha (OKA), and Tarama (TRA). According to reports, some mileage runners booked up to a staggering 12 flights per day, leaving few empty seats on some essential flights.

Sources indicate that at Miyako Airport, some passengers were observed arriving with just small handbags, and then immediately heading to the departures area to board their next flight. As a few travelers explained:.

It has been revealed that the concern is that this mileage running reportedly created serious difficulties for locals, who depend on the island flights for medical appointments, shopping, and other essential travel. There were some successive days in February where flights between Miyako and Tarama were booked out in advance, leaving locals unable to book seats. Here’s what some locals had to say:.

Tarama Mayor Mitsuo Iranami even called on mileage runners to consider the impact their activities were having on the island community, commenting “I would like those doing mileage runs to understand the situation on remote islands and exercise some consideration, taking into account the number of people participating.”.

Japan Airlines reportedly even introduced measures intended to counteract this, including offering full refunds without cancellation fees, along with 500 bonus miles as an incentive. Below is a news story in Japanese about this, so you can watch that with subtitles, if you’d like.

I think this story is a good reminder of just how well frequent flyer programs can work with the purpose of filling seats on planes… for better or worse!

While it’s fairly common to see loyalty programs offer promotions, nowadays it’s rare to see deals that are actually that lucrative. When it does happen, we sometimes see that the people behind the promotion clearly didn’t think through all possible scenarios, and this is one of those situations.

While Japan Airlines’ double status points promotion in February is pretty standard, the airline has added a latest restriction for the offer this coming year, by capping the number of bonus points that can be earned during the promotion period, presumably to prevent something like this from happening.

Obviously I feel bad for the locals in this situation, but it’s also hard to blame frequent flyers here for simply taking advantage of a promotion as advertised.

Japan Airlines’ Mileage Bank frequent flyer program ran a promotion that might have just done too good of a job getting people to book flights, as a double Life Status Points offer caused some people to book up to a dozen flights per day, with some flights reportedly having up to 80% of passengers be mileage runners.

Ordinarily that would be considered a success in terms of filling planes, but the matter here is that mileage runners descended on island routes that are also a lifeline for residents, given the efficiency of flying there. It’s not often you hear a mayor make a plea with mileage runners, but that’s exactly what happened here.

#122787. Breaking: FCC pick advanced by Senate Commerce after Democratic boycott

📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: FCC pick advanced by Senate Commerce after Democratic boycott

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (887 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks with reporters after the Senate luncheons in the Capitol on Tuesday.
  • The fight over partisan balance on the Federal Communications Commission snarled a Senate markup Wednesday morning as Republicans advanced a controversial nomination despite a Democratic boycott in an attempt to deny a quorum.
  • Republicans on the Commerce Committee voted unanimously to advance the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, a senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to be a member of the commission, alongside several transportation and communications bills.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks with reporters after the Senate luncheons in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

The fight over partisan balance on the Federal Communications Commission snarled a Senate markup Wednesday morning as Republicans advanced a controversial nomination despite a Democratic boycott in an attempt to deny a quorum.

Republicans on the Commerce Committee voted unanimously to advance the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, a senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to be a member of the commission, alongside several transportation and communications bills.

The fate of the nominations and bills could ultimately be decided via a challenge on the Senate floor, according to a Democratic committee staffer, speaking on condition of anonymity.

In a statement Wednesday morning, committee Democrats, led by ranking member  Maria Cantwell of Washington, said they objected to Thumann Severs’ nomination without a Democratic “pair” nomination and referenced a letter they sent to Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, on Monday requesting the nomination be removed from the agenda.

“Commissioner Anna Gomez could be re-nominated with all swiftness, as we have called for numerous times,” the group wrote. “This is not a problem we created, but a problem that the White House can solve.”.

Thumann Severs, if confirmed, would give the FCC three Republican members and one Democrat, Gomez. The three Republicans could then constitute a quorum on the commission, allowing President Donald Trump to potentially fire Gomez. The commission generally has five members, three of the president’s party and two in the minority.

Cruz noted at the markup that there is nothing in the law that requires moving nominees in pairs, and that committee Republicans would continue their work on what he called a nomination that followed a “typical process.”.

In a recent development, “Democrats will control the Senate, unfortunately, in January,” Cruz said. “But today is November 18th. The American people elected each of us to fulfill our duties, including advice and consent, for our full terms.”.

Related: Threats to broadcasters hang over FCC nominee hearing.

The Democratic staffer told reporters that because the committee did not adopt rules at the beginning of the 119th Congress, it has been operating under rules from the 118th, which required the attendance of at least one member of the minority party to constitute a quorum for reporting bills or nominations.

“The remaining recourse is to basically go to the floor and . . . make an inquiry in terms of what took place today, and then there would have to be a formal ruling by the chair,” they mentioned.

They added that in determining whether the committee had a quorum to advance the nomination, “It would depend on how they view our committee rules from the 118th that we practice under for the 119th versus what the Senate rules are.” The staffer noted they have not yet spoken with committee Democrats or Democratic leadership about plans for such an inquiry.

Democrats also previously boycotted a committee markup in March over an aviation safety bill left off the committee’s agenda, after which action was deferred. The committee later came to agreement and rescheduled the markup.

In their letter Monday, Democrats quoted Cruz from a 2014 statement about the nomination of Loretta Lynch to be attorney general.

“As you wrote in 2014, controversial nominees ‘should not be confirmed in the lame duck session of Congress by senators who just lost their seats and are no longer accountable to the voters.’ We agree,” the letter said.

On Tuesday, Sen. Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., wrote his own letter to Cruz calling for the removal of the nomination from the agenda based on grounds that Thumann Severs lied to the committee.

Sources indicate that “While Ms. Thumann testified she did not work ‘on any media-related problems,’ documents obtained through Freedom of Information Act requests demonstrate that she worked on several media related issues, including on commitments that Skydance made to pave the way for FCC approval of its merger with Paramount,” Luján wrote.

Democrats have criticized the FCC and Carr for allowing media consolidation, including by Skydance. There has also been bipartisan criticism of Carr’s threats against broadcasters for speech he disagrees with.

Luján told reporters Wednesday prior to the markup that he expects, under Democratic control next year, Carr and potentially Thumann Severs would be called to testify.

“I have questions. I certainly hope that Brendan Carr will voluntarily show up to this committee when invited, and that other rules and tools do not need to be used,” Luján stated, responding to a question about possibly subpoenaing Carr. “But . . . everything should be on the table.”.

Sources indicate that sen. Jerry Moran, R-Kan., remarked at the markup that he spoke with Thumann Severs about her role at the FCC and her “lack of engagement” as the commission has made decisions regarding broadcasters. He also said he found her testimony at last week’s nomination hearing “comforting.”.

“I have concerns with FCC action in regard to political speech, broadcasters, and she indicated in her answers . . . in a way that provided me with a level of comfort about her nomination in regard to that problem,” Moran said.

Moran also said he hopes to meet with Thumann Severs before her nomination is brought to the floor.

    In a recent development, A McDonnell Douglas MD-11, operated by FedEx Express, overran a runway upon arrival at Miami International Airport (MIA) on Wednesday. The incident triggered the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to impose a ground stop, putting a wrench in the peak of the Thanksgiving travel rush.

    Industry observers note that it is unclear what may have caused the trijet to veer off the runway, but weather radar indicated rain at the time of landing. It comes less than three months after an Amazon Prime Air-branded Boeing 767-300F overran a runway at MIA, killing five people.

    In a recent development, MIA has become fully operational, with all flights allowed to resume. However, delays are estimated to be nearly four hours. Over 530 flights were reported to be delayed as of 11:40 PM.

    Miami is the third-most popular tourist destination for Thanksgiving, according to Washington Examiner journalist Anna Giaritelli​​​​​​.

    Miami and surrounding areas were dealing with harsh rain conditions around the time of FX910's arrival. The weather in southeast Florida was described as a "black hole," according to Washington Examiner journalist Anna Giaritelli, who reportedly received a text from an off-duty air traffic controller minutes before the MD-11 landed at MIA.

    Industry observers note that "All the southeast traffic landing miami, lauderdale etc has basically ran into a black hole of weather. Commpand center didn't help us with routes, we lost our land lines to communicate with other facilities, over 10 sever(e) turbulence reports," they explained. "This was absolutely the most dangerous operation I've seen.".

    Industry observers note that video of the incident obtained by speedbirdHD indicates the aircraft passing by on the runway. It appears the crew deployed the aircraft's reverse thrusters, attempting to slow down before overrunning the runway.

    It has been revealed that fedEx confirmed the incident in a statement to Simple Flying on Wednesday. The company said it will coordinate with authorities as the investigation begins.

    “FedEx Flight 910 from Memphis to Miami experienced an concern upon landing Wednesday evening at Miami International Airport. We are grateful that our crew is safe and there are no reported injuries. We are coordinating closely with investigating authorities, and any additional questions should be referred to the FAA.”.

    The ground stop was planned to last until 9:45 PM, according to CBS News. Around 9:40 PM, the FAA stated the airport would "shortly" become operational again.

    "Flights will be resuming shortly at Miami International Airport after FedEx Flight 910 ran off the runway after landing," the agency remarked. "The McDonnell Douglas MD-11 departed from Frederick W. Smith International Airport in Memphis. There are no reports of injuries. The FAA will investigate the incident.".

    Sources indicate that at around 10:45 PM, MIA was gradually accepting some arriving flights via Runway 27 and Runway 30. However, several dozen flights were seen stuck on the tarmac awaiting departure clearances.

    Industry observers note that MIA officials confirmed that Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units responded to the incident, and there were "no reported injuries." The extent of the damage to the aircraft is unclear. However, the airframe's fuselage did not separate, according to Enilria, indicating that severe external damage may not have been sustained.

    Simple Flying contacted FedEx late Wednesday, but representatives could not be immediately reached for comment.

    Recent findings suggest that the FAA issued a ground stop at MIA as a result of the runway excursion. The order, however, did not close all runways at the airport. In a statement on social media, MIA officials noted all runways were "closed except for runway 9R." The airport also encouraged passengers to check with their airlines for any impacts to flights departing Wednesday night.

    Recent findings suggest that "Passengers scheduled to travel tonight are encouraged to check directly with their airlines for the latest flight updates before heading to the airport," it noted. "We appreciate our passengers’ patience as we work to safely resume normal operations.".

    According to initial reports from aviation blogger Enilria, the MD-11 overshot the runway at around 8:15 PM after landing amid rain showers at MIA. Flight tracking data indicates the flight, FX910, was operated by N605FE, from FedEx’s hub at Frederick W. Smith International Airport (MEM). The airframe is 34 years old, according to ch-aviation.

    According to recent reports, the flight pushed back at 4:55 PM local time and took off from MEM at approximately 5:17. Just 20 minutes after departure, the aircraft reached its cruising altitude of 37,000 feet. It maintained the altitude for about an hour and 10 minutes, traveling south, before beginning its descent. At around 6:55 PM EST, data highlights the aircraft making a sharp turn southeast as it continued descending through 33,000 feet. It then flew directly toward MIA for about 15 minutes before turning directly east to pass north of the airport.

    Industry observers note that the plane continued east, passing the coastline, and descended further. It turned back around west to line up for final approach at around 8:17 PM. The aircraft touched down on Runway 26R nine minutes later at 8:26 PM, but failed to stop before overshooting the runway, according to reports.

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1515 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    The Forgotten Pacific Airfield Where WWII Fighter Jets Are Being Reclaimed By The Jungle

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1515 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, it is well known that many World War II fighter wrecks lie across the islands of the Pacific.
    • Sources indicate that while various Japanese bunkers, radio buildings, light-rail trains, and guns are found across Palau, most of the fighting is on the smaller island of Peleliu.
    • The island of Yap was controlled by Spain until the Spanish-American War of 1898, when it lost Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Philippines, and Guam to the United States.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, it is well known that many World War II fighter wrecks lie across the islands of the Pacific. Many of these are lost, forgotten, or abandoned, left to rot in jungles. Others lie in shallow waters, becoming refuges for marine life and attractions for today's divers. In October and November, I visited the island nations of Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia FSM (Yap Island), where the remains of WWII are everywhere. Only a very limited number of rather niche divers seem to be the only true tourists Yap attracts today.

    Sources indicate that while various Japanese bunkers, radio buildings, light-rail trains, and guns are found across Palau, most of the fighting is on the smaller island of Peleliu. Unfortunately, I didn't visit Peleliu, although I did visit Yap. Peleliu was the site of one of the deadliest Marine operations. Conversely, invasion plans for Yap were scrapped, and the island was bombarded and bypassed. Today, visitors can see Japanese WWII aircraft lying, reclaimed by the jungle where they were destroyed.

    The island of Yap was controlled by Spain until the Spanish-American War of 1898, when it lost Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Philippines, and Guam to the United States. Spain was left with a large expanse of small Micronesian islands that the United States did not take over but could not defend. It promptly sold the islands to the emerging German Empire.

    According to recent reports, as World War I broke out, Japan promptly seized most of the German Pacific islands, although Australia took Nauru and Upcoming Guinea and New Zealand took German Samoa. The former German islands were then run by Japan under the League of Nations South Seas Mandate. It appears from Japanese colonization of the islands that Japan planned to integrate these islands, including Yap, into Japan proper, although this never happened.

    It has been revealed that when the Pacific War broke out, Japan had managed Yap for around 35 years and was busy populating the island. During the war, it fortified the islands to create a defensive ring to defend the Japanese home islands. The US Navy released its famous island-hopping campaign to bring its bombers within range of the home islands. For a brief period of time in 1944, Yap found itself at the center of the Pacific War.

    The Japanese military buildup on Yap began relatively late, and it was not heavily fortified before the Pacific War. The island lacked a good natural harbor and had few natural defensive strong points. The most significant Japanese installation was the airfield at Lamer, located adjacent to the modern Yap International Airport.

    The runway was built using reef material, although locals told me that the Japanese also used thousands of their famous money stones (Rai). By April 1944, the main strip was completed while some of the supporting infrastructure was unfinished. The site's main purpose was to establish an air transit and staging point for Japanese aircraft moving across the region. The combined Japanese Army and Navy garrison on the island totaled around 4,000 to 5,000 men.

    Recent findings suggest that the US had intended to invade the island, but instead opted for bombing, neutralizing, and bypassing it. By May and June, Japan was deploying aircraft to the island. American reconnaissance reported 24 Japanese fighters, six dive bombers, two medium bombers, and six night fighters. The aircraft soon became a target for American long-range B-24 bombers. By September, Americans were encountering little or no aerial resistance from the island.

    Recent findings suggest that after the war, the bombed-out Japanese airfield appears to have been abandoned. The forests regrew and reclaimed the airfield, while locals treated the runway as a roadway and built their homes along it. Today, some Japanese wrecks are located next to homes. Visitors can go and explore the old airbase and find the wrecks, as I did. There are World War II marker signs at most of the notable wrecks, but some are not marked. The signs are often not maintained and can be lost over time.

    Industry observers note that almost all the land on Yap is privately owned, and visitors are expected to ask landowners for permission before seeing the wrecks, even if they are marked and signed. In all, I found the wrecks of around eight Japanese aircraft, including a Mitsubishi G4M 'Betty' bomber. Bizarrely, the Betty bomber now lies next to a Boeing 727 that crashed next to it decades later.

    Industry observers note that the runway is in poor shape, and it is extensively potholed and overgrown. It is lined with abandoned cars rotting in the jungle. Yap may be famous for its stone money, but having explored the island, it is hard not to also associate it with endless abandoned, decaying cars. Aircraft wrecks can generally be found between 150 and 300 feet (45 to 91 meters) from the runway.

    The Mitsubishi G4M bomber is one of the most notable wrecks. It was a medium bomber/torpedo bomber, with Japan building 2,435 examples of the type. It had a crew of seven. Another notable wreck is a Japanese Nakajima B5N Torpedo Bomber. These were three-man carrier-based torpedo bombers, of which Japan built 1,149 units. A number of Mitsubishi A6M Zero fighters can also be found.

    I found two small tails of wrecked aircraft that I assumed were Zeros, but they were unmarked, and I couldn't tell for sure. The Google Maps screenshot above marks the locations on the old airfield where I found Japanese wrecks. There are likely many more to be found, but this is private land, and the jungle is extremely thick, making movement and visibility very difficult.

    Japanese aircraft on Yap (per 1944 US reconnaissance).

    Sources indicate that all around the airfield, large bomb craters from US bomb strikes are visible. I am used to finding these bomb craters in Vietnam. Many are visible at Vietnam's historic site of My Son, but they always seem to be difficult to make out in photos, especially when they are surrounded by thick jungles. One of the aircraft wrecks I found was next to a bomb crater, and I had to climb in and out of the crater to get around what was left of the aircraft.

    Recent findings suggest that across the island, I saw many other remains of WWII. These include a well-marked Japanese Type 88 75mm anti-air gun preserved next to some Zero fighters. On the main hill overlooking the main settlement of Colonia, I found four more Japanese guns with the barrels destroyed. These were marked, but they are overgrown, and the signs have largely disappeared.

    According to recent reports, lost on the island is a Japanese lighthouse that became target practice for American pilots. A bomb disposal unit that happened to be on the island revealed me pictures of it; I looked for it but failed to find it. But perhaps the most notable other wrecks are the remains of US Vought F4U Corsair fighter planes and B-24 bombers. These are typically less well-preserved, with sometimes just the engine or propellers remaining.

    Recent findings suggest that I saw some houses with propellers on display, presumably from US or Japanese bombers. Two propellers are on display at Pacific Missionary Aviation's (PMA) hangar at the main airport. I asked the pilot about them; he said one was a US B-24 propeller, and the other was a B-29. US aircraft wrecks tend to have memorial plaques for the pilots, although they are not maintained and are decaying. Memorial plaques are absent from Japanese wrecks.

    In a recent development, the WWII wrecks are a mixture of abandoned, forgotten, marked, and commemorated. Particular attention has been given to locating and commemorating American aircraft. One plaque I found tells the tale of Lt. Zack F. Lillard and the remains of his F6F-5 Hellcat that he operated from the USS Enterprise CV-6. It reads, "Following the war, Zack's body and the wreckage were not found, and he was declared missing. The partial wreckage of his plane was located in 2008.".

    It has been revealed that it's clear an effort was made in the 2000s to locate and mark the wrecks, but many of these signs have been left abandoned. It should be noted that there are practically no tourists on Yap. Foreigners on Yap are almost exclusively on business, government, military, or diving. The divers I saw didn't seem interested in exploring the island. I was the only backpacker on the island, and expats there told me they rarely or never see such tourists visiting Yap.

    It has been revealed that when I was on Yap, I met and had drinks with a bomb disposal group made up mostly of contracted retired US military personnel. Their task was to find and gather unexploded WWII ordnance and blow it up. They informed me that they found and removed live rounds from aircraft pictured in this article, although I am not sure exactly which ones. That long-abandoned ammo was detonated while I was exploring the island looking for WWII wrecks.

    Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    Sources indicate that saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen. Bernie Sanders said Wednesday that he would prioritize passing the universal health care proposal if he assumes the chairmanship of the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee next year as expected.

    According to recent reports, democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters. And the idea could be buoyed by an influx of progressive lawmakers elected in the midterms.

    In a recent development, sanders said Medicare for All is gaining support from voters across the country who are looking to overhaul the American health care system as costs have soared. Democrats on the committee will move the legislation “as aggressively as we can, as rapidly as we can,” he said.

    Sources indicate that his version, introduced in April and referred to the Senate Finance Committee, would implement the universal health care system over four years. In the first year, the the age of Medicare eligibility would drop to 55 from 65, while coverage would expand to include dental, hearing and vision care. The bill would also provide coverage for eligible children during the first year.

    The age of eligibility would fall another 10 years in each of the following years until the fourth year, when coverage would be extended to all Americans.

    “If there has ever been a time in the modern history of our country . . . to address the crises facing working families, this is that time,” Sanders stated, noting that Democrats will have a 56-44 majority when the 120th Congress begins in January, the largest margin for either party in 16 years.

    According to recent reports, sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., along with nine other Senate Democrats, last week offered an alternative Medicare expansion plan, which would lower the eligibility to those ages 50 and up.

    While who will be leading Senate Democrats is still an open question — Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is challenging Charles E. Schumer of New York, who has been the top Senate Democrat since 2017 — Sanders said he is confident the Medicare for All bill will get to the Senate floor, “no matter who the [Senate majority] leader is.” Sanders previously expressed opposition to Schumer leading the conference.

    Asked about efforts to extend the Affordable Care Act enhanced subsidies, Sanders responded he’s “all in.” However, he added “the American people and elected officials understand the current health care system is broken.”.

    Subsidies that help enrollees pay for health care premiums on the ACA exchanges were expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic, but these enhanced credits expired at the end of last year, raising costs for many who relied on them to help defray costs.

    Sources indicate that house Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, nominated on Wednesday to be speaker next year, previously outlined broader health care priorities such as extending the ACA tax credits and reversing Medicaid cuts enacted in Republicans' reconciliation package last year. When asked Tuesday how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that’s all part of an ongoing conversation.”.

    Industry observers note that in addition to expanding Medicare coverage, Sanders reiterated his push to lower prescription drug prices. The Vermont lawmaker previously introduced legislation aimed at reducing the cost of brand name prescription drugs by linking domestic prices to international price benchmarks.

    To enact some of the agenda, Sanders may have to court Republicans.

    Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., stated last week that he plans to serve as the top Republican on the HELP committee next year. Sanders said Wednesday that his likely GOP counterpart “has shown an enormous amount of courage in taking on Republican leadership year after year.”.

    Sanders added that although Paul may have a different viewpoint from himself on committee issues, he looks forward to finding common ground.

    Fascinating Air Saint-Pierre Domestic Transatlantic Flight Returns In 2027

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that one of the most interesting transatlantic flights will be returning yet again in 2027.
    • Industry observers note that in the summer of 2018, an interesting domestic transatlantic route released — it operated seasonally once weekly.
    • In a recent development, what’s Saint Pierre and Miquelon?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that one of the most interesting transatlantic flights will be returning yet again in 2027. Maybe this will be the year I finally get to try it, even if there’s no premium cabin angle!

    Industry observers note that in the summer of 2018, an interesting domestic transatlantic route released — it operated seasonally once weekly. Specifically, ASL Airlines operated a Boeing 737-700 that was marketed by Air Saint-Pierre between Paris (CDG) and Saint Pierre and Miquelon (FSP).

    In a recent development, what’s Saint Pierre and Miquelon? It’s a self-governing territory of France, situated in the northwestern Atlantic Ocean, near Newfoundland and Labrador. The islands cover an area of about 93 square miles, and have a population of just about 6,000 people.

    The territory’s airline, Air Saint-Pierre, only has turboprops, which the carrier flies to places like Halifax (YHZ), Montreal (YUL), and St. John’s (YYT). Obviously these planes aren’t capable of operating across the Atlantic, so the airline leases a Boeing 737 for the once weekly flight.

    This was the first time ever that we saw a nonstop link between these territories and mainland France. There were some other things that made this route interesting:.

    The route ended up returning in 2019, was then paused in 2020 and 2021 due to the pandemic, and then returned in 2022 through 2026. The route will now be returning yet again, for the 2027 season, so it sure seems like this is basically a permanent thing.

    The once weekly flight between Saint Pierre and Miquelon and Paris will be returning in 2027, between June 21 and September 6, 2027.

    According to recent reports, the route will once again be operated by an ASL Airlines France Boeing 737-700, and the flight will be marketed and sold by Air Saint-Pierre. The flight will operate westbound on Mondays and eastbound on Tuesdays, as follows:.

    Paris to Saint Pierre and Miquelon departing 4:00PM arriving 6:30PMSaint Pierre and Miquelon to Paris departing 10:30AM arriving 8:05PM.

    The 2,664-mile flight is blocked at 6hr30min westbound and 5hr35min eastbound. As you can see, the plane sits on the ground in Saint Pierre for quite a while. This is so that the crew can get their rest and operate the flight back the next day, rather than making them stay there for over a week.

    Sources indicate that I imagine the airline is able to get a decent deal on parking at the airport for 16 hours. 😉 It’s also interesting since this is an eastbound daytime transatlantic flight, which is fairly rare.

    If you want to book a seat on this flight, below is the pricing for travel in both directions, with fares starting at €660 one-way for standard adult fares.

    Industry observers note that as you can see, the fare difference just comes down to the age of the traveler, as well as the level of flexibility you’d like, with fares either being non-refundable and non-changeable, non-refundable but changeable for a fee, or refundable and changeable. The plane is in an all-economy configuration, as there’s no premium cabin.

    Air Saint-Pierre will be bringing back its flight between Saint Pierre and Paris in the summer of 2027, operated by ASL Airlines. This is an absolutely fascinating route, and it’s so cool to see that it was launched in the first place, and is sticking around.

    In a recent development, while the link between Paris and this French territory is obvious, it’s still kind of awesome that such a small territory can support a flight like this. But I guess the downside was fairly limited, since the route was subsidized from the beginning. Personally I find this to be the most intriguing transatlantic route.

    Southwest Priority Card Review: Strong Airline Benefits For Frequent Flyers

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Southwest Airlines has several co-branded credit cards with Chase.
    • Sources indicate that this is my in-depth Southwest Priority Card review, covering the card’s benefits.
    • Link: Learn more about the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Southwest Airlines has several co-branded credit cards with Chase. Of the three personal cards, my favorite one is the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card.

    Sources indicate that this is my in-depth Southwest Priority Card review, covering the card’s benefits. I’ll also explain how despite this being the highest annual fee personal card in the portfolio, I still think it represents the best deal. Now is also a good time to consider applying for the card if you’re a fan of Southwest’s popular Companion Pass perk.

    Link: Learn more about the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card.

    Before I review the Southwest Priority Card benefits in detail, here’s a high-level look at everything you need to know about the card:.

    Here are my thoughts on the Southwest Priority Card’s main pros and cons:.

    If you’re thinking about applying for the Southwest Priority Card, you’re probably most interested in the welcome bonus it’s presently offering, along with its annual fee and general eligibility rules for getting the card. So let’s dive into those. I’ll also explain a recent change to how Southwest cards factor into qualifying for the Companion Pass, which pertains to all cards, not just the Priority.

    The Southwest Priority Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus: Earn 90,000 bonus points after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. This is higher than the standard welcome offer for the card, and its minimum spending requirement should be easy for most spenders to meet.

    Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, and based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Rapid Rewards points to be worth 1.2 cents each. So, to me, the points from this welcome offer are worth $1,080.

    Industry observers note that chase and Southwest have some pretty strict rules when it comes to who is eligible for the card. The Southwest Priority Pass is not available to anyone who currently has a Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card, or anyone who has received a welcome bonus on a Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card in the past 24 months. However, you are eligible if you have a Southwest business credit card.

    This is in addition to Chase’s general application rules, including the 5/24 rule, whereby you typically won’t be approved for a Chase card if you’ve opened five or more new card accounts in the past 24 months. However, that’s not enforced consistently.

    When it comes to credit scores, there’s not a consistent score that you need to get approved for the card, though I’d hope to have a score in the “excellent” range. That being said, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected, as it’s one of only many factors that determines card eligibility.

    Recent findings suggest that the Southwest Priority Card has a $229 annual fee. As a point of comparison, the other personal cards have annual fees of $99 and $149, so the annual fee on this card is a bit higher. However, as I’ll explain below, the benefits could justify the premium annual fee.

    The card also has no extra cost to add authorized customers, so you can add those for $0 each, so that authorized user spending can help you rack up rewards.

    Industry observers note that the Southwest Priority Card has no foreign transaction fees, so this could be a useful card for your spending abroad. This is a Visa as well, and Visas are accepted pretty widely around the globe.

    Another rule worth mentioning here involves how Southwest credit card welcome bonuses help you earn the Companion Pass, which lets you bring a companion with you on flights (both cash and award tickets) and pay just taxes and fees.

    Industry observers note that for a long time now, the points earned as part of Southwest credit card welcome bonuses have counted towards the 135,000 qualifying points needed to earn the Companion Pass. But starting soon, credit card welcome bonuses will no longer count toward qualification.

    You’ll need to apply for a card by December 2, 2026, for your welcome bonus to count toward the Companion Pass for a final time. So apply for the Priority Card sooner rather than later if you’re hoping to earn that perk with the help of credit card spending.

    Industry observers note that now is also your last chance to get an annual boost of 10,000 Companion Pass qualifying points as a Southwest credit card holder. Starting next year, instead of a boost of 10,000 TQPs for having a Southwest card, you’ll get 10,000 TQPs if your TQP balance is 130,000 by December 31, 2027. That would be enough to get you to Platinum status, which will include unlimited Companion Pass trips as a benefit.

    This change eliminates the easiest way to earn this valuable benefit, and it’s not the only fresh rule: referral bonuses, anniversary points, bonus points from spending, and partner spending won’t count toward the Companion Pass either. In fact, Southwest’s rolling the Companion Pass into its highest elite tier, Platinum, and requiring either 140,000 TQPs or 100 qualifying flights to earn it.

    Beyond the Southwest Priority Card airline benefits, a major draw is the card’s points earning on every purchase you make — plus how it can help you work toward Southwest elite status through earning Tier Qualifying Points.

    The Southwest Priority Card offers the following points for credit card spending:.

    In a recent development, personally, I’d generally only put spending on the card if you’re going for A-List status and/or Companion Pass, because there are better cards for everyday spending otherwise. But still, those are some fairly solid bonus categories.

    As part of an overhaul of the Rapid Rewards program, Southwest is simplifying TQP earning on credit cards. Starting in 2027, every dollar spent on a co-branded Southwest credit card will earn you one TQP. In other words, $35K in spending would earn you Silver, $65K in spending would earn you Gold, and $140K in spending would earn you Platinum.

    This earning rate is the same across cards, so this isn’t specific to the Southwest Priority Card.

    I have a dedicated post that covers how to redeem Southwest Rapid Rewards points for maximum value, but let’s briefly look at how you can use the points you earn from the Southwest Priority Card.

    Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, meaning that the value you get from your points is tied to the cash cost of Southwest tickets. There are a few different levels, ranging from Basic tickets to Choice Extra fares, so the exact value can vary a bit.

    According to recent reports, basic award fares tend to offer the best redemption value. You’ll also usually get the best value on international Southwest routes to destinations like Costa Rica and Aruba. I’ve been able to get about 2.0 cents per point on these redemptions.

    According to recent reports, starting in spring 2027, Southwest will add points earning and redemption opportunities with select airline partners, which should make your Rapid Rewards points more valuable for international travel. The planned partners include Icelandair, China Airlines, and Etihad Airways — I look forward to seeing how these add value to the program.

    One great thing about the Southwest Rapid Rewards program is that there are no change or cancellation fees, and rebooking a fare when the price drops gets you a refund equal to any difference in points. Just note that Basic fares can only be changed by upgrading to a higher fare bundle, so for a cheaper Basic award you’d cancel and rebook rather than change.

    It has been revealed that as Southwest’s highest annual fee personal credit card, the Southwest Priority Card has the most benefits, including several that can improve your travel experience with the airline. Here are the card’s most notable ongoing perks.

    Southwest Priority Card holders can select a Preferred seat on Southwest at the time of booking for no extra charge. If Preferred seats aren’t available on your flight, you should be able to select a standard seat for free. Preferred seats are located near the front of the cabin, so having one usually means you’ll board and deplane faster.

    Preferred seats generally cost about $30 to $60 extra, and selecting free Preferred seats at booking is a perk of Southwest Silver elite status. If you don’t have status and you’re able to use this benefit, you could get real value even after just a few Southwest flights.

    Recent findings suggest that the Southwest Priority Card also offers unlimited upgrades to extra legroom seats within 48 hours prior to departure. This perk applies to the main cardholder as well as up to eight additional passengers on the same reservation.

    According to recent reports, extra legroom seat prices vary by route, but they generally cost roughly $40 to $100. On a route where they’re at the higher end of this range and you have multiple companions on your reservation, you could even recoup the Priority Card’s annual fee through one trip alone.

    Keep in mind that complimentary extra legroom seats within 48 hours of departure is another benefit of Southwest Silver status. So if you have that level of status or higher already, you don’t need the Priority Card to enjoy this perk.

    The Southwest Priority Card gets the primary cardholder and up to eight additional passengers on the same reservation a first checked bag at no additional cost. Checked bags on Southwest cost $45 each way, so this can save you up to $90 roundtrip on checked bag fees per person.

    With even a couple of roundtrip flights per year, this benefit can offset the annual fee — and about five one-way checked bags per year could cover it as well.

    With the Southwest Priority Card, you’ll be able to board with Group 5, or earlier if you have elite status or a fare or seat type that qualifies you for an earlier boarding group.

    Sources indicate that southwest has eight total boarding groups, so while there are several ahead of Group 5, it’s better than boarding last. This benefit applies to the main cardholder and up to eight passengers on the same reservation.

    In a recent development, on your Southwest Priority Card anniversary every year, you’ll receive 7,500 bonus Rapid Rewards points. Southwest Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, and you can generally expect that you’ll need around 83 Rapid Rewards points for every dollar of airfare you book.

    It has been revealed that in other words, 7,500 bonus points get you around $90 in Southwest airfare annually. That covers more than a third of the annual fee right there.

    If you pay with your Southwest Priority Card you can save 25% on inflight Wi-Fi and drink purchases. You’ll receive statement credits for the 25% within two billing cycles of your purchase (though usually much faster than that).

    The Southwest Priority Card offers a variety of travel & purchase protection benefits, including:.

    Of course, you’ll want to check the cardmember agreement for the full terms & conditions associated with these benefits.

    Even though the Southwest Priority Card has the highest annual fee of any personal Chase Southwest card, it might be worthy of consideration.

    Many people love flying Southwest for the ability to earn the Southwest Companion Pass, the lack of change fees and vouchers that don’t expire. For others, Southwest is just a practical airline to fly on occasion, given its massive route network. Regardless, there’s lots of value in having points and benefits on Southwest.

    Recent findings suggest that that remarked, not everyone needs a Southwest credit card — and even among Southwest credit cards, there’s a cheaper option that could make more sense if you only fly the airline a few times a year. Let’s look at some alternatives and how they stack up.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, this article was updated on Thursday, November 26, 2026, to include a statement from British Airways and the aircraft's current status.
    • A British Airways Boeing 787-10 Dreamliner declared an emergency over the North Atlantic on Tuesday night after reporting an engine oil leak.
    • Recent findings suggest that despite a recommendation by the airline's operations team to divert to Iceland, the pilots managed to continue to Boston Logan International Airport (BOS), where the plane landed safely.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, this article was updated on Thursday, November 26, 2026, to include a statement from British Airways and the aircraft's current status. It was originally published on Wednesday, November 25, 2026.

    A British Airways Boeing 787-10 Dreamliner declared an emergency over the North Atlantic on Tuesday night after reporting an engine oil leak. The aircraft (G-ZBLC) — powered by two Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 engines — was operating flight BA239 from London Heathrow Airport (LHR) when it squawked 7700 more than four hours into the flight.

    Recent findings suggest that despite a recommendation by the airline's operations team to divert to Iceland, the pilots managed to continue to Boston Logan International Airport (BOS), where the plane landed safely. The incident comes just ten days after the same aircraft shut down an engine over the Mediterranean and diverted to Athens. Tuesday's flight to Boston was the airframe's first flight back in service since the Athens diversion.

    Sources indicate that flight tracking data shows that BA239 departed Heathrow just after 7:30 PM local time on Tuesday evening, and was over four hours into its roughly eight-hour journey to Boston when the pilots squawked 7700, indicating a general emergency. The Boeing 787-10 was cruising at around 33,000 feet and traveling at 378 knots when it declared the emergency.

    Boeing 787-10 Dreamliner (G-ZBLC).

    Declared an emergency after an engine oil leak. Landed safely in Boston.

    Sources indicate that air traffic control recordings reveal that the pilots stated the problem was due to an engine oil leak. The pilots told Gander Air Traffic Control in Canada that the jet was losing oil when the engines were running at high power, and once they lowered the thrust, the oil leak stopped getting worse. The crew then descended to 28,000 feet and kept the engines at lower power for the remainder of the flight.

    As reported by X account Flightdrama, ACARS messages during the emergency show that British Airways' maintenance had recommended a diversion to Keflavik (KEF) in Iceland. The messages also indicated that the same jet had previously experienced an oil leak concern, in reference to a diversion incident just ten days prior to Tuesday night's incident.

    According to recent reports, BA239 ultimately landed safely in Boston at 10:55 PM EST, around an hour after its scheduled 9:50 PM arrival. Flying lower and slower than planned (at under 400 knots, compared with a typical cruise speed close to 500 knots) added time to the journey. It remains to be seen whether authorities will open an investigation into the emergency.

    In a recent development, the aircraft involved, G-ZBLC, experienced an engine shutdown emergency on November 14, while it was operating BA105 from Heathrow to Dubai International Airport (DXB). The widebody was roughly three hours into the flight when the crew shut down the right-hand engine and diverted to Athens (ATH).

    According to The Aviation Herald, a passenger on the flight reported that the pilots confirmed the cause of the diversion as an oil leak, although this has not been confirmed by the airline. However, ACARS messages during Tuesday night's incident cited a previous oil leak during a diversion, suggesting this did happen.

    Unlike on BA105, Tuesday's pilots did not shut down an engine, instead managing the problem by reducing thrust. Tracking data demonstrates the aircraft remained on the ground in Athens for six days, until it was repositioned back to Heathrow on November 20. It then stayed in London for another four days before re-entering service on Tuesday with the flight to Boston.

    Recent findings suggest that G-ZBLC first flew in September 2020 but was not delivered to British Airways until December 2022, after being caught up in Boeing's prolonged pause in 787 deliveries over production quality complications. It operated its first revenue flight on December 23, 2022, to Denver International Airport (DEN).

    BA's 787-10s can seat up to 256 passengers across four cabins and operate long-haul routes to destinations including Boston, Newark, Seattle, Nairobi, Lagos, and Dubai. With a total of 44 Dreamliners in its fleet, the carrier is one of the few airlines globally to operate all three variants, namely the 787-8, 787-9, and 787-10.

    Another of the airline's 787-10s was involved in a mishap this month after getting stuck in the mud at Heathrow ahead of a flight to Lagos. The jet was taxiing towards the runway when it failed to complete a left turn and ran onto the grass verge, with its nose landing gear sinking into the ground.

    Industry observers note that the aircraft remains out of service in Boston since Tuesday's incident. The aircraft was scheduled to return to Heathrow as BA238 at 7:30 AM on Wednesday, less than nine hours after arriving, but the flight was canceled. British Airways has also commented on the incident. In a statement to Simple Flying, a spokesperson for the airline mentioned:.

    Recent findings suggest that "The aircraft arrived safely in Boston and customers disembarked as normal. Safety is always our highest priority.".

    The airline said the flight crew identified a "minor technical issue" and followed established procedures. It also apologized to passengers for their late arrival in Boston. However, the carrier did not offer any details on what caused the oil leak, or whether the problem was linked to the one that forced the Athens diversion ten days earlier.

    • Recent findings suggest that fifty years later, Alexander S.C.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that sen. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., speaks during a ceremony marking the restoration of Alexander Calder’s Mountains and Clouds sculpture in the Hart Senate Office Building atrium on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    The day after Alexander Calder presented his plan for a public art display in the Hart Building’s nine-story atrium to the Architect of the Capitol, he died.

    Recent findings suggest that fifty years later, Alexander S.C. Rower felt a sense of awe as he stared up at his grandfather’s work, finally restored to what he had envisioned.

    According to recent reports, “It’s totally phenomenal,” he remarked, pointing up at the now-moving clouds as he spoke, spinning his finger around. “It’s not entertainment, but it’s trying to emulate naturalness, trying to emulate what nature would do.”.

    Industry observers note that it was a long time coming for Rower, who remembers traveling to the Capitol in his 20s for the original dedication of the Mountains and Clouds sculpture in 1987. The mobile portion stopped rotating as Calder intended in the 1990s, and it was ultimately removed in 2014 after being deemed unsafe by the Architect of the Capitol. Millions of dollars in private philanthropy later, Calder’s clouds are spinning again.

    Industry observers note that rower was back on the Hill on Wednesday for an event celebrating the restoration, joining Architect of the Capitol Thomas Austin, Sens. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., Angus King, I-Maine, and James Lankford, R-Okla., and the project’s donors. As the speakers addressed the crowd, the clouds began to speed up slightly. Onlookers gathered on the balconies overlooking the atrium and peeked through office windows. Attendees left with tote bags emblazoned with images of Calder’s art.

    According to Rower, who leads the Calder Foundation dedicated to preserving and interpreting his grandfather’s art, the mobile is rotating on a 15-hour cycle that is “totally variable.”.

    Recent findings suggest that “It can go a little faster; it can go a little slower,” he said. “I told the team today that during lunchtime, I want it to speed up just a little bit because everyone’s going to lunch. There’ll be … a lot of activity passing through, and then right at 2:30, well, let’s make it go quieter.”.

    It was a labor of love for those involved, and not an inexpensive one. Jon and Kim Shirley funded the $12 million restoration. Because the pieces were so large, they were transported on an extra-wide load truck and driven at a speed of 35 miles per hour from Michigan.

    “We had to call every senator or governor that we knew on that route, which went through seven states, to get permissions,” he stated. “That was a huge thing to overcome, and it all happened over a weekend. So my wife was actually on the phone with a governor’s wife on Saturday evening. The next day, he called up his Department of Transportation and got a permit.”.

    Christian Quilici, who helped manage the project on behalf of the Shirleys and said he serves as a liaison between the foundation and Congress, said the hardest part of the project was the size of it.

    “We had to tear the wall down on C Street, which nobody really thought of in the beginning,” he said. “Nobody got how big this was until it showed up on their doorstep.”.

    Quilici said he spent years educating at least 30 different senators about the quest to reunite the mobile with the stationary mountains left behind. Some of the biggest champions were seated in the front row at Wednesday’s event, including Senate Democratic Whip Richard J. Durbin. Absent was Sen. Christopher S. Murphy, D-Conn., who has been away from the Capitol while recovering from a stroke but has been a supporter of the sculpture’s restoration for years, pressing former acting Architect of the Capitol Joseph DiPietro on it at a 2024 Senate Legislative Branch Appropriations budget hearing.

    “Is there any chance that before I leave the Senate, or at least before I die, we can get the clouds back up there?” Murphy remarked at the time.

    Padilla read a letter on Wednesday from Murphy, whose state was Calder’s home for much of his life.

    Industry observers note that “This statue is actually a statement on our democracy, that we have significant pieces of monumental art right in the middle of our most important and most iconic government buildings. To get this piece of art restored to how it was designed by the artist, well, that’s good for Connecticut. But I also like to think … it’s good for democracy too,” Murphy’s statement said.

    The restoration was funded entirely by donations from the Shirleys, who are prominent Calder collectors, according to Rower.

    According to recent reports, “It’s very emotional to see the work completed after 10 years of us working so hard with the Architect of the Capitol and Calder Foundation. It’s a very overpowering, overwhelming emotion,” mentioned Kim Shirley.

    In addition to helping fund the project, she’s a former Senate staffer who worked in Hart before Calder’s work was installed. Years after her time in the Senate was over, her husband Jon wanted to show her the sculpture, now filling the space she used to walk through every day.

    But when the two arrived, the clouds weren’t hanging from the ceiling like they were supposed to be. He called up Rower, who was a friend of his, and said he wanted to get them back to how Calder intended. On Wednesday, the three of them stood together in Hart, looking up.

    Technological and engineering advancements allowed for newer, lighter clouds to be built and be safe to hang from the ceiling.

    “Before it was like a bulb, it looked like a hoagie sandwich, and now it looks just really sharp, like a razor cutting through space, which was Calder’s intention,” Rower noted.

    According to recent reports, according to Rower, it involved laser-measuring the original model of Mountains and Clouds sitting in a glass case nearby in the Hart atrium. The new clouds, he said, are made of carbon fiber.

    “These are giant things up in the air, and they’re just so gentle and subtle,” he mentioned.

    Younger Hill staffers don’t know a time with clouds. But for those who have spent decades in the building, it was a special moment to see them spin, as Lankford told the crowd.

    “I can’t tell you how many tour groups that I’ve walked through this building and I pointed to this, and I said it’s only half there, and would take them over to the little model that’s right over here, and say this is what it’s supposed to look like,” said the senator, a former Hill staffer himself.

    Standing under his grandfather’s sculpture, Rower found himself quoting the man responsible for it all.

    “I find that everything I do, if it is made for a particular spot, is more successful,” he remarked, gazing up at it.
