    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Rove’s Black Friday Deals Offer Up To 55% Transfer Bonuses—Plus 10x On Hotels That Earn Points And Perks

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5067 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Rove is offering up to 55% more miles when you transfer to five airline and hotel programs, along with 10 miles per dollar on hotel bookings that still earn hotel points, elite night credit and status benefits.
    • For the hotel offer there’s no stay deadline, so you can book future travel on Black Friday and collect the higher earning rate.
    • Rove is a standalone rewards program.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rove is offering up to 55% more miles when you transfer to five airline and hotel programs, along with 10 miles per dollar on hotel bookings that still earn hotel points, elite night credit and status benefits. For the hotel offer there’s no stay deadline, so you can book future travel on Black Friday and collect the higher earning rate. Rove is a standalone rewards program. You earn its miles through travel bookings, shopping, dining and gift cards, then redeem them for travel or transfer them to airline and hotel programs. There’s no particular credit card you need to carry. Most of these offers last just one day. Here’s the schedule Rove gave me: November 26–30: transfer bonuses and double referral bonuses, ending at 11:59 p.m. Eastern on Monday, November 30. Black Friday, November 27: the 10x Loyalty Eligible hotel offer, boosted shopping and gift card earnings, first hotel booking bonus and double qualifying miles. These end at 11:59 p.m. Eastern that night. 40%–55% Transfer Bonuses To Five Programs The same percentage bonus applies to Japan Airlines Mileage Bank, Air France KLM Flying Blue, Finnair Plus, Copa ConnectMiles and ALL Accor. Your Rove status determines the percentage. The four airlines normally transfer 1:1. Accor’s normal ratio is 1.5 Rove miles to 1 Accor point. Here’s what transferring 15,000 Rove miles gets you: Rove Status Bonus Airline Miles Or Avios Accor Points Member or Gold 40% 21,000 14,000 Platinum 50% 22,500 15,000 Diamond 55% 23,250 15,500 Those percentages already include the extra transfer bonus for Platinum and Diamond. Japan Airlines is worth looking at for its own flights and partner awards, including American Airlines and Alaska Airlines itineraries with three free stopovers. Rove offered everyone a 50% Japan Airlines transfer bonus in October, though. The 40% offer for most members is lower than that, while Diamond’s 55% is higher. Japan Airlines miles expire after 36 months, so a bonus doesn’t make them a good place to park miles indefinitely. Finnair is useful even if you don’t plan to fly Finnair. You can move Avios to British Airways at 1:1. Your Finnair account needs to be at least 30 days old before you can link it to another Avios program. Accor points are generally worth 2 euro cents each toward eligible hotel stays. The 15,000 Rove miles in the table therefore produce €280, €300 or €310 in hotel value, depending on status. Platinum effectively gets a 1:1 transfer to Accor during this promotion, and Diamond does slightly better. 10x Hotel Miles While Keeping Hotel Points And Benefits On November 27, new Loyalty Eligible hotel bookings earn 10 Rove miles per dollar. Rove indicates there are no property or rate exclusions within that category, and no promotional deadline to complete the stay. I’ve liked this feature since it introduced. You can earn Rove miles while retaining hotel program points, qualifying nights and applicable elite benefits, along with the rewards from the card you use to pay. A $1,000 qualifying room subtotal earns 10,000 Rove miles. At 1.5 cents per mile, that’s $150 in additional travel value, before the hotel and credit card rewards. 5,000 Miles On A First Hotel Booking Has Different Rules Promo code BF500 adds 5,000 Rove miles to an eligible first Rove Rate hotel booking of $500 or more made on Black Friday. Join if you aren’t already a member and then take advantage of this. Rove clarified that you must never have booked a hotel through them before. Someone who’s already made a Loyalty Eligible reservation doesn’t qualify merely because this would be their first Rove Rate booking. An existing Rove account can qualify if it hasn’t booked a hotel. The code can combine with an eligible Rove elite hotel discount. However, Rove Rate bookings don’t earn hotel points or elite night credit, or guarantee hotel elite benefits. At exactly $500, the bonus adds 10 Rove miles per dollar to the booking’s standard earnings. I’ve covered a 5,000 mile first booking offer at the same spending threshold before. Double Qualifying Miles Includes Purchased Miles Boost Black Friday transactions that ordinarily earn qualifying miles will earn twice as many toward Rove status. Rove confirms that includes purchased Miles Boost and elevated earnings for elite members. For example, $1,000 in qualifying hotel spending at the promotional 10x rate generates 10,000 redeemable miles and 20,000 qualifying miles. The extra status credit doesn’t double the redeemable miles you can transfer or spend. Rove’s annual requirements remain: Gold: 50,000 qualifying miles and 5 qualifying transactions. Platinum: 125,000 qualifying miles and 10 qualifying transactions. Diamond: 250,000 qualifying miles and 20 qualifying transactions. Flat bonuses such as BF500’s 5,000 miles don’t ordinarily qualify, so they aren’t part of the doubling. Status earned for 2026 lasts through December 31, 2027. Travel counts toward the year it’s completed, while shopping and gift card purchases count by purchase date. A hotel stay ending in 2027 won’t be 2026 qualifying activity because it was booked in 2026. Higher Gift Card Earnings And The Full Shopping List Rove is offering up to 30% more miles on nearly all gift cards on Black Friday. A 30% increase would turn a 5x rate into 6.5x, for instance. (The actual rate depends on the gift card.) Rove sells gift cards marked for instant mileage earning which can help with this weekend’s transfer bonuses. Store Standard Rate Black Friday Rate SPanel 44x 50x Surfshark 29x 35x Upwork 26x 30x Bizzbox 20x 30x ExpressVPN 20x 30x Rocket Lawyer 16x 20x FreedomGPT 16x 20x LightPDF 14x 25x WinRAR 12x 20x Malwarebytes 12x 20x Peet’s Coffee 11x 15x Kate Spade Up to 9x Up to 10x Kate Spade Outlet Up to 9x Up to 10x StubHub 7x 10x Fanatics 7x 9x iHerb 6x 8x Walgreens 5x 6x Anthropologie 5x 7x Zenni Optical 5x 10x Under Armour 4x 11x Athleta 4x 7x Shein Up to 3x Up to 11x Sephora 3x 5x ULTA Beauty 3x 5x Total Wine & More 3x 4x LOFT 3x 5x Gap 3x 5x Petco 3x 7x Express 3x 5x Old Navy 2x 5x Nike 2x 4x Apple 2x 3x Kohl’s 1x 3x Double Referrals And A Points Consultation Giveaway From November 26 through November 30, Rove is doubling the standard member referral payout to 1,000 miles per qualifying referral plus 10% of the referred member’s earnings for their first six months, with a requirement that the new member earn at least 250 bonus miles. You can join Rove and then you’re welcome to leave your referral link in the comments though note that this link is good for 1,500 points just for joining rather than the standard 500.     Breaking: Tempers flare as future of Social Security debated

    • Ron Johnson, R-Wis., remarked he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).
    • If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday highlighted how poisonous the politics could become.
    • Budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., remarked he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday highlighted how poisonous the politics could become.

    Budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day. Democrats erupted, accusing Johnson of scaring seniors and being unwilling to fix a financial lifeline for more than 72 million retirees.

    “I think it’s outrageous,” said Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., one of several Democrats on the panel who slammed Johnson for his comments. “Don’t go out there scaring Americans to make political points on Fox News. This is too fricking important.”.

    Johnson acknowledged making an “imprecise comment” on prospects for a fix during the Fox interview. But he also told Democrats that if they had read his “chairman’s memo” he sent them Tuesday they would know he wants to preserve the system and pass a law to prevent any cuts to benefits if the Social Security Trust Fund is depleted.

    "This is a scam, it’s grotesque, and at this point there’s really no way to fix Social Security," he said on Fox Business. "It’s a Ponzi scheme. You can’t fix it. You just shut it down and hope you can recover some of your money.”.

    But Johnson appeared to contradict himself later in the same interview, saying there is a difference with a “government-sanctioned Ponzi scheme” in that “you can force investors to keep putting money into it and that’s what we’ll probably have to do … You can fix Social Security and make it solvent.”.

    In his opening statement at the hearing, Johnson noted Congress should pass a law to prevent benefit cuts and then “roll up our sleeves and begin seriously addressing the main problem, our massive debt and deficits.” He said that is the only way to “ensure we have the financial wherewithal to honor promises made to seniors.”.

    Johnson also told the panel he used the term “Ponzi scheme” in part to draw attention to the importance of addressing the problem. “If I gotta pay a political price for that, I really don’t care,” he said.

    Industry observers note that there is no doubt that a fix is needed. Without any change, Social Security recipients face a 22 percent cut in benefits by the end of 2032, according to projections from the Social Security Board of Trustees. Johnson stated Congress and the president won’t cut benefits even if the trust fund is exhausted.

    And there has been no shortage of Social Security bills introduced to provide a fix, but none of them has gained momentum.

    According to recent reports, sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, drew flak from fellow Republicans after he and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., proposed lifting the cap on income subject to the Social Security payroll tax so that the tax would apply to all earned income.

    A bipartisan proposal, from Sens. Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., Bill Cassidy, R-La., Tim Kaine, D-Va., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, would have put a plan in motion by requiring the Social Security Advisory Board to recommend a bill that would ensure Social Security is funded for at least the next 50 years.

    According to recent reports, senators on both sides of the aisle said they were committed to fixing Social Security. Republicans stressed the importance of economic growth to bring in more revenue to the system and cautioned that tax increases would slow growth.

    Democrats pitched shifting more revenue into the system, for example by raising the cap on the payroll tax or taxing other income.

    “I do believe if we can be focused on fixing the Social Security stability concern, that could be a stepping stone to fixing broader problems,” said Kaine, who is anticipated to chair the Budget Committee when Democrats take over Congress next year.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Marriott Bonvoy has just revealed its status soft landing policy for the next membership year, and it’s good news (well, at least for those who don’t requalify for their current status tier).

    According to recent reports, marriott Bonvoy has just revealed its status soft landing policy for the 2027 status year, for situations where someone doesn’t qualify for a particular elite tier based on their activity in 2026. Specifically, elite members who don’t achieve the published criteria to maintain their status will only drop down at most one elite tier.

    In other words, Ambassador Elites will at most drop to Titanium Elite, Titanium Elites will at most drop to Platinum Elite, Platinum Elites will at most drop to Gold Elite, and Gold Elites will drop at most to Silver Elite.

    In a recent development, for what it’s worth, this policy matches Marriott’s historical approach to status soft landings. Before Marriott and Starwood merged, back when Marriott’s loyalty program was named Marriott Rewards, Marriott consistently had a status soft landing policy. With this, Marriott Rewards members never dropped more than one elite tier per year, regardless of their activity.

    That policy has continued since the new program was formed, including for the next year. However, there’s no guarantee this will continue to be the policy in the future. For those curious, the status offered as part of the soft landing also does count toward lifetime elite status. So if you’re downgraded from Titanium to Platinum based on a soft landing, that year of Platinum will add to your total.

    During the pandemic, we saw airline and hotel loyalty programs largely extend elite status several times. This made sense, given the extent to which business travel decreased for many. However, with the huge increase in leisure travel and all the latest ways to earn elite status, we’ve seen elite ranks swell.

    According to recent reports, personally I think the concept of a status soft landing makes a lot of sense. After all, sometimes life conditions change for people, and in many cases those changes are just temporary. If you drop from top tier status to no status, you don’t really have much of an incentive to stay loyal to that hotel group when your travel picks up again.

    Industry observers note that by offering a soft landing, loyalty programs can try to build more of a long term relationship with members, and that’s a positive. We also see some programs allow members to pause their status for a year or extend status as a one-time exception based on life circumstances, and I think that’s a great policy as well.

    It has been revealed that marriott Bonvoy has a generous status soft landing policy for 2027, for those who don’t requalify for status in 2026. If you didn’t requalify for your current status tier with Marriott Bonvoy in 2026, you can expect that you’ll be downgraded at most one status level.

    #122760. Chase Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card Review: Are The Benefits Worth The Fee?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2718 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Chase Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card Review: Are The Benefits Worth The Fee?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card is one of the most compelling co-branded airline credit cards out there.
    • In a recent development, so this post is my in-depth Air Canada Aeroplan Card review.
    • Link: Learn more about the Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card is one of the most compelling co-branded airline credit cards out there. I’m a huge fan of the Air Canada Aeroplan program — even if you have no connection to Air Canada or Aeroplan, the program is fantastic for partner redemptions, and this card is worth being aware of. And if you do fly Air Canada with any frequency, the perks for travel on the airline are strong.

    In a recent development, so this post is my in-depth Air Canada Aeroplan Card review. Let’s go over all the details, and discuss if the card is worth it.

    Link: Learn more about the Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card.

    Before I review the Air Canada Aeroplan Card benefits in detail, here’s a high-level look at everything you need to know about the card:.

    Here are my thoughts on the Air Canada Aeroplan Card’s biggest pros and cons:.

    According to recent reports, if you’re thinking about applying for the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card, you’re probably most interested in the welcome bonus it’s at the moment offering, along with its annual fee and general eligibility rules for getting the card. So let’s get into those details.

    Sources indicate that the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card currently has the following welcome bonus: Limited Time Offer: Earn up to 80,000 bonus points. Earn 60,000 bonus points after you spend $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months your account is open. Plus, up to 20,000 more bonus points by earning 50% more bonus points per $1 spent on purchases that normally earn 1 bonus point in the first 2 months from account opening..

    Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Aeroplan points to be worth 1.4 cents each. That means the 80,000 points are worth $1,120 to me. However, even if you have a different valuation of these points than I do, you can at least use the “Pay Yourself Back” feature to redeem these points for 1.25 cents each toward a travel purchase, so that’s a pretty high “cash out” value.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is issued by Chase, and has pretty standard application restrictions:.

    While Chase doesn’t have a public credit score requirement for the Air Canada Aeroplan Card, you’ll have the best chances of approval if your score is in the good range or higher. That roughly translates to a minimum score of 670. However, people have been approved with lower scores and rejected with higher scores, as it’s one of only many factors that determine card eligibility.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card has a $195 annual fee. There’s no cost to add authorized users to the card, and their spending will count toward your points balance and any spending thresholds.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s a great card to use globally, and possibly even earn bonus rewards on your spending depending on what you’re using the card for.

    Recent findings suggest that the Air Canada Aeroplan Card has a well rounded rewards structure, among the most interesting you’ll find on any airline credit cards. This isn’t just about the number of points that you earn, but also about the additional rewards for spending. Specifically, the Aeroplan Card offers the following:.

    In a recent development, those are some excellent bonus categories. For what it’s worth, the card offers 1x Aeroplan points on all other purchases, so there are better cards for everyday spending.

    It has been revealed that there’s a lot to love about Air Canada Aeroplan points, even if you don’t usually fly Air Canada or travel to Canada. Among other things:.

    It has been revealed that I redeem miles through Aeroplan all the time, and consistently get great value. Booking award flights on Air Canada itself rather than other partners isn’t always the best deal, though, especially if you’re booking during a peak travel time, since Air Canada awards use dynamic pricing.

    It has been revealed that the Air Canada Aeroplan Card gives cardmembers plenty of opportunities to earn elite status with Air Canada Aeroplan. You get some status outright just for being a cardmember, and you can earn further status with spending.

    According to recent reports, those who are approved for the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card receive Aeroplan 25K status. This is valid for as long as your account is open. Aeroplan Elite 25K is Air Canada’s entry level status, and includes travel perks with Air Canada, including:.

    Each year, those with the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card also receive 5,000 Status Qualifying Credits (SQCs) to help work toward the next level of Aeroplan status. This is automatic, but as I’ll cover below, you can stack additional credits on top through hitting certain spending thresholds in the calendar year.

    For those curious, below are the Aeroplan elite requirements.

    Beyond the automatic 5,000 SQCs you’ll receive each calendar year just for having the Air Canada Aeroplan Card, you can earn up to 20,000 additional credits by hitting spending thresholds. Here’s how that breaks down:.

    So you can earn a total of 25,000 SQCs each calendar year through the Air Canada Aeroplan Card.

    Whether or not that’s worth it really depends on how much you fly Air Canada, and what the opportunity cost of your credit card spending is.

    Those with the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card can get a one-tier status upgrade to Aeroplan 35K status when they spend $75,000 on the card in a calendar year. You’ll get status for the remainder of the calendar year you qualify and the entire following calendar year.

    If you ask me, the value here is really for someone who is actually loyal to Air Canada. Aeroplan 35K status gets you three complimentary checked bags on Air Canada flights (vs. just one with Aeroplan 25K), 10 eUpgrade credits, and a 3x elite points multiplier on eligible Air Canada or Star Alliance flight bookings, among other things.

    Sources indicate that the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a variety of valuable benefits and credits, beyond the elite status perks covered above. Some of these benefits are offered just for being a cardmember, while others can be earned with spending. The perks are pretty comprehensive, and you’ll find almost everything you could want short of lounge access. So let’s go over those.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers up to $100 in Air Canada statement credits when you make qualifying Air Canada purchases. The credits apply to paid airfare, taxes and fees on award flights, and inflight food and drinks, though onboard Wi-Fi is excluded.

    This breaks down as two credits of up to $50 each, one from January 1 through June 30 and one from July 1 through December 31. If you book cash fares on Air Canada twice a year, this is an easy way to put $100 back in your pocket, and this benefit alone can cover about half of the card’s annual fee.

    As an Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card holder, you can receive a 15% discount on the Aeroplan points required to book an award flight on Air Canada, Air Canada Express, or Air Canada Rouge. In practice, this also seems to work on partner award flights, as long as at least one segment is on Air Canada. The upside here can be absolutely huge, and it’s a great reason to have this card.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a free first checked bag on Air Canada flights for the primary cardmember and up to eight others traveling on the same itinerary. This applies to itineraries with Air Canada, Air Canada Rouge, or Air Canada Express. The value of that could add up pretty quickly. There’s no need to actually pay for the ticket with the card, as long as you’re the primary cardmember and have your Aeroplan number linked to the reservation.

    Recent findings suggest that once every four years, the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a credit that’s valid toward a membership with Global Entry, TSA PreCheck, or NEXUS, worth up to $120. These are all programs that can save travelers time at the airport, and potentially even at the border.

    I specifically love that the card also offers a NEXUS credit, since that’s historically something we haven’t seen card issuers offer. NEXUS is arguably the best of the three programs, since it gets you access to Global Entry, TSA PreCheck, and expedited immigration in Canada.

    Industry observers note that admittedly this is probably more interesting in theory than in practice, but I still like where Aeroplan is going with this. Those with the Air Canada Aeroplan Card will automatically have carbon offsets purchased for their flights when redeeming Aeroplan points for an Air Canada flight.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is a World Elite Mastercard, which comes with certain perks, including a concierge service and presale tickets for eligible events.

    While you’ll want to consult the cardmember agreement for full details, the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a variety of travel protection when paying with the card, including the following:.

    Sources indicate that there’s another feature that you’ll find on the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card, which isn’t available on any other airline card. Specifically, the Aeroplan Credit Card offers a Pay Yourself Back feature, whereby cardmembers can apply their Aeroplan points toward travel purchases on any airline, hotel, or rental car, at the rate of 1.25 cents per point, up to 200,000 points per year.

    This is an incredibly innovative concept, and something that cardmembers may find to be valuable. So whether you want to redeem your points for a stay at a Four Seasons or a flight on JetBlue, the possibilities are endless. It’s also a reason to potentially think of the welcome bonus differently — the bonus points earned with the welcome offer can over time be redeemed toward any recent purchase or even toward the card’s annual fee.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card also offers the ability to earn priority reward vouchers. Each can be used to get 50% off an eligible Aeroplan award ticket, and is valid for travel on Air Canada or a partner airline.

    You earn these vouchers at the following four annual spending thresholds:.

    These can each be used in the same way, and the value depends on your status:.

    As you can tell, the value here will depend on your status and travel patterns, but there’s potentially quite a bit of value to be had.

    While this is something that most people won’t be able to achieve, I love the concept behind this, and for some it might just be the best deal in travel. The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers what I’d consider to be the world’s most valuable companion certificate, for those who spend a million dollars per year on the card.

    If you reach that threshold, you’ll receive an award redemption companion voucher that’s valid globally:.

    In a recent development, we’ve never seen a credit card offer a perk quite this valuable before. Obviously, the spending requirement is massive here, and this would only make sense if you were planning a lot of travel in a particular year. For a certain type of consumer, though, this is an incredible opportunity.

    A few Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card benefits are set to expire on December 31, 2026, so they won’t be around for too much longer. Here’s a quick look:.

    If you already have the card, now is your last chance to take advantage of these perks. Especially with the 10% transfer bonus, it’s worth seeing if an Aeroplan award flight makes sense with your upcoming travel plans so you can get some extra value for your rewards before this perk retires.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is an innovative product with a big welcome bonus, great return on spending, and valuable perks. That’s just about all that I look for in a credit card.

    Airline co-brand credit cards are extremely popular given the allegiance many people have to a particular airline. Admittedly Aeroplan is at a disadvantage in the US market, since not as many people in the US are loyal to Air Canada as they are to American, Delta, or United, for example.

    Sources indicate that that being stated, I think the thoughtful value proposition of this card more than makes up for it for Air Canada loyalists. If you like to redeem points for international premium cabin awards, it could be worth applying for this card. Similarly, the card can be worth it for the Pay Yourself Back feature, whereby you can redeem your Aeroplan points however you’d like toward a travel purchase.

    Hopefully most people find value beyond just the bonus, given the excellent rewards structure.

    Arguably the biggest challenge with the Aeroplan Credit Card is how easy Aeroplan points are to earn with other cards that provide more flexibility. Aeroplan is transfer partners with several bank currencies, including Amex Membership Rewards, Bilt Rewards, Capital One, and Chase Ultimate Rewards, and all those currencies can be converted at a 1:1 ratio.

    That means the points are pretty easy to come by, and in many cases there are compelling value propositions on those cards as well.

    If you’re under 5/24, consider these two cards from Chase:.

    If you’re over 5/24, these are some other top Aeroplan Card alternatives to consider:.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is phenomenal, and easily the most innovative co-branded airline credit card we’ve seen. The card offers a nice welcome bonus, a lucrative rewards structure with a variety of incentives for spending, and comes with great perks, like elite status.

    The Aeroplan program is rewarding in general, but if you don’t fly Air Canada or book award flights through Aeroplan more than once or twice a year, you might want to consider earning flexible points that transfer to this program instead.

    Learn more about the Aeroplan Credit Card.

    Industry observers note that booked a discounted UA short-haul economy flight for my son and me, using miles from P2's (UA CC holder) UA account. Since she isn't on the same reservation and I have 25k status through the Aeroplan CC, I used my Aeroplan member number in the hope that we can get a free checked bag each.

    According to recent reports, so, booking an award flight every 6 months effectively brings the annual fee back down to $95. It's just too bad the partner awards have really dried up. 3x earn rate on travel is decent, but with an occasional transfer bonus the 2x rate on Sapphire Preferred becomes 2.5x if you really want Aeroplan points.

    In a recent development, for Canadian residents going for high AC status, ignoring this card will cost you. Canadian readers know: AC high status is vital, if you don't want to pay hundreds of thousands of points for longhaul. One needs to earn SQCs. This card's SQC earn rate is higher, compared to the top-tier Canadian AC cards (TD VIP, CIBC VIP, Amex Reserve) so the 25k is faster, cheaper to get. I keep TD VIP for lounge, additonal cardholder benefits, but I keep the Chase card for the easier SQC earn. It's easily worth the CAD$270.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, A newly elected congressman is getting mocked for refusing a TSA face scan, with commenters telling him to take the bus or train instead.
    • The democratic socialist gets some of the explanation wrong.
    • Rabb, a Pennsylvania state representative, was elected to represent Philadelphia in Congress and takes office in January.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, A newly elected congressman is getting mocked for refusing a TSA face scan, with commenters telling him to take the bus or train instead. The post sharing his video accuses him of refusing to have identification. But Chris Rabb claims he brought a U.S. passport card, which is accepted ID. And the checkpoint photograph he declined is optional. The democratic socialist gets some of the explanation wrong. However, the people demanding his arrest appear to have a bigger problem with the rules than he does. Rabb, a Pennsylvania state representative, was elected to represent Philadelphia in Congress and takes office in January. In the video, he says he’s returning to Philadelphia from Boston. He says he doesn’t have a REAL ID card. He got a passport card so he wouldn’t need to carry his actual passport. He says TSA’s equipment wouldn’t process his identification, employees asked for another ID, and he didn’t have one with him. He also says he’d told them he didn’t consent to the photograph. DSA Congressman Chris Rabb already working for the people by refusing to let TSA take his photo and also refusing to have an ID card. So brave. https://t.co/DnZSKeKZ7e — Lee Kuan Yimby (@LeeKuanYimby) November 23, 2026 He Brought A Type Of ID TSA Accepts The State Department says a U.S. passport card can be used for domestic air travel instead of a REAL ID driver’s license. It fits in a wallet. It doesn’t work for international air travel, but Boston to Philadelphia isn’t international. REAL ID enforcement doesn’t mean every passenger needs a state license with a star. A passport, passport card, and other documents on TSA’s accepted identification list are acceptable. Ye replies include “Arrest his ass,” “poor Comrade,” “Bro just ride the train,” and sarcastic declarations of bravery. I have plenty of disagreements with democratic socialists. I’ve criticized Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s intervention in American Airlines’ maintenance dispute and Bernie Sanders getting airline taxes wrong. That doesn’t make a socialist’s privacy objection wrong. And disliking someone’s glasses isn’t a reason to demand he surrender a choice even the government says he has. You Can Decline The Photo. You Still Have To Complete Screening. Rabb’s most useful advice is simple: Just say, “I don’t consent to being photographed.” That’s TSA’s published policy. Travelers can decline facial recognition and use the standard ID verification process instead. Rabb Wants To Avoid Being Put In A Database Rabb says he’s trying to avoid being put into another database. Too late! The standard checkpoint camera compares your face to the photograph on the ID you present. TSA says the image isn’t saved after a positive match, apart from limited testing used to evaluate the technology. You don’t necessarily have to believe them. Touchless programs can work differently. Identifying an enrolled traveler using a gallery of existing government photographs doesn’t add you to the database, you’re already there. Opting out doesn’t remove your travel records. The government already receives passenger information for Secure Flight screening. And obtaining a passport card already means you supplied a photograph. There are cameras everywhere, but for the most part there’s so much data that at least we benefit from security through obscurity. At least we did before AI made it all so much more easily searchable. I’ve covered passenger information collected for aviation security being used to help immigration agents intercept travelers. Law enforcement has access to passenger data even without this additional photo. Positive ID Matches Don’t Contribute Much To Security Positive identification is supposed to make sure you can’t simply fly under somebody else’s name. That’s necessary for the government’s database of people they want to bar from flying or ensure receiving extra screenig works. Of course, the database itself is corrupted. The terrorist screening database has over two million people in it. I’ve written about the sprawling watchlist system and agents using the no fly list to retaliate against people who wouldn’t become informants. Identity checks also serve a separate economic purpose for airlines. Matching the traveler to the name on a nontransferable ticket helps enforce price discrimination. If you could buy a cheap ticket months ahead and freely sell it to someone traveling tomorrow, you’d compete with the airline’s expensive last-minute fare. Preventing that resale helps airlines separate passengers willing to proposal ahead from those willing to pay more. It doesn’t create a real aviation security benefit. I Made My Own Compromise Long Ago I’m an old line civil libertarian on this. I was late signing up for Global Entry in 2013 because I didn’t like volunteering fingerprints and a photograph to the government in exchange for easier travel. When I finally joined, before the Edward Snowden revelations, I was already writing about government collection of cellphone geolocation data, license plate readers, and other surveillance. The government already had the information, so I might as well get the benefits. At the same time, I think we’ve largely lost this argument in practice. I’ve written about the spread of checkpoint photography and biometric boarding gates becoming normal. The surveillance state has won. Rabb himself concedes that his refusal won’t make much practical difference. He sees value in reminding people they can object and in resisting normalization. I have sympathy for this. What To Do If You Want To Opt Out Bring an accepted physical ID and make the request before the camera takes your picture. “I’m opting out of the facial photograph. Please use the standard ID check.” Hand over the document and cooperate with that check. Separate a camera objection from a document problem. If the reader won’t process a passport card, ask for a supervisor and an alternative document check. Carrying a second accepted ID can save time if something fails. With millions of passengers processed per day small failure rates mean actual failures happen regularly. Escalate a refusal of the opt out calmly. TSA says you can request a supervisor or passenger support specialist. Record the airport, checkpoint, date, time, and what was mentioned, and submit a complaint. They’ll go ahead and ignore or dismiss it. Don’t confuse any of this with arriving without allowable identification. Since February, TSA’s ConfirmID requirement costs $45. The payment covers a ten day travel period and doesn’t guarantee identity verification. Meanwhile, at the border, U.S. citizens can request an alternative inspection. Noncitizens, including permanent residents, generally cannot claim the same photo opt-out. Rabb will shortly have a better tool than an argument at a document podium: a seat in Congress. He can press for enforceable limits on retention and sharing, a meaningful manual alternative, and a way to challenge bad database entries. It won’t matter, because the security state is far more powerful than he is. But I’d be happy to see a democratic socialist spend some of his time constraining government power over travelers. They’ll go ahead and ignore or dismiss it. Don’t confuse any of this with arriving without allowable identification. Since February, TSA’s ConfirmID requirement costs $45. The payment covers a ten day travel period and doesn’t guarantee identity verification. Meanwhile, at the border, U.S. citizens can request an alternative inspection. Noncitizens, including permanent residents, generally cannot claim the same photo opt-out. Rabb will shortly have a better tool than an argument at a document podium: a seat in Congress.     #122757. KLM Offloaded A Passenger Rather Than Use The Blocked Seat We Offered

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (803 w)

    KLM Offloaded A Passenger Rather Than Use The Blocked Seat We Offered

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (803 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I recently flew KLM from Amsterdam to Barcelona, and a passenger was taken off our full flight even though my wife and I offered him the empty seat between us.
    • Business class inside Europe is basically a regular economy seat with the middle seat blocked.
    • I was on KL1519 on 2 September, in row 2 with my wife, with that empty middle seat between us.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I recently flew KLM from Amsterdam to Barcelona, and a passenger was taken off our full flight even though my wife and I offered him the empty seat between us. The crew followed a rule exactly, and as far as I can tell, nobody got anything out of it.

    Business class inside Europe is basically a regular economy seat with the middle seat blocked. On some planes the middle seat is physically blocked with a small table. On this flight it was just empty, blocked online so nobody could book it, but technically a regular seat anyone could sit in.

    I was on KL1519 on 2 September, in row 2 with my wife, with that empty middle seat between us.

    After the doors closed, it turned out that two passengers had boarding passes for the same seat. Whoever got there first sat down. The other one was a fairly young guy, and now he had nowhere to sit. The flight was completely full, there wasn’t a single free seat in economy.

    I heard the crew apologizing to him and saying they would have to take him off the plane and put him on the next flight.

    According to recent reports, I knew this would take a while, because the doors were already closed and he had boarded. Getting him off meant opening the doors again, and maybe taking his bag off too. Once on another flight someone got off and everyone had to hold up their bags.

    And I felt sorry for the guy. Maybe he was in a hurry to get somewhere, and none of this was his fault. The airline gave two people boarding passes for one seat, and he was already on board.

    It has been revealed that so I asked my wife if she minded giving up the empty seat between us. The flight is only about two hours. She was fine with it, so I went to the crew and offered it.

    The crew was very grateful, but said seating someone there was against the rules and they couldn’t decide it themselves, they had to check with someone.

    That took about 10 minutes. Then they came back, thanked me again, and noted that unfortunately it wasn’t possible under the rules.

    So they opened the doors and offloaded the guy, I hope they rebooked him on the next one. In the end we pushed back about 40 minutes late and landed in Barcelona about half an hour late. After landing I think even the captain came over, shook my hand and thanked me.

    Industry observers note that as I understand it, the middle seat is blocked to give the business class passengers more space. In this case that was us, and we were the ones offering to give that space up.

    We didn’t need the space, and we’d have put up with one more person in the row for two hours.

    On a completely full KLM flight, two passengers got boarding passes for the same seat. My wife and I offered the empty blocked seat between us in business, so he wouldn’t have to get off. The crew checked with someone, the answer was no, and he was offloaded anyway, and we left about 40 minutes late.

    I get that the crew couldn’t make this call themselves. Still, we didn’t need that seat at all.

    Is there a good reason for this rule that I’m missing?

Perhaps they couldn't figure out how to technically show someone as being "loaded" on the flight, given that the middle seats don't have a corresponding seat in the system. As far as the GDS knows, those middle seats aren't blocked, but instead, they just don't exist.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Malaysia Airlines has just placed a new aircraft order, as the airline will be adding a new wide body aircraft type to its fleet. This seems logical enough, even if the carrier’s long haul fleet seems rather diversified at this point.

    It has been revealed that malaysia Airlines has placed its first-ever Dreamliner order, as the airline will be taking delivery of up to 16 Boeing 787-10s. This includes a firm order for 10 jets, plus options for six more, with deliveries expected between 2032 and 2035.

    For context, the 787-10 is the largest variant of the Dreamliner. While it has the least range of any 787 variant, the per-seat economics are great, given how it’s “stretched.” While some airlines have started to use the 787-10 for high capacity regional routes, Malaysia Airlines is taking a different approach.

    It has been revealed that the oneworld carrier intends to use these planes to support its long haul fleet modernization and international expansion, including routes to Europe, along with destinations throughout Asia-Pacific. The airline points out how long haul demand to and from Southeast Asia has increased by more than 50% over the past decade.

    Here’s how Malaysia Airlines Group CEO Nasaruddin Bakar describes this:.

    Sources indicate that “The acquisition of the 787 Dreamliner represents a strategic investment in the future of Malaysia Aviation Group. As we look ahead to the next phase of growth, these aircraft will strengthen our ability to serve key international markets with greater capacity, efficiency and flexibility, while delivering the elevated travel experience our customers expect. Beyond fleet renewal, this investment reinforces our commitment to maintaining a modern, competitive airline that supports Malaysia’s connectivity and global aspirations.”.

    In a recent development, for context, Malaysia Airlines at the moment has a fleet of just over 90 aircraft, with another 75 aircraft on firm order. As it stands, Malaysia Airlines has:.

    Now the airline has the following planes on firm order:.

    Industry observers note that A few things stand out here. First of all, it’s cool to see Malaysia Airlines growing again, after a rather rough… what, nearly 15 years? At this point the airline has enough planes on order to both replace its previous generation fleet, and expand. I’d expect the 16 A330ceos will be retired at some point in the coming years, and more than replaced by the A330neos that remain on order. Furthermore, the 737-800s will all be replaced by the 737 MAXs.

    The 787-10 is an incredible plane in terms of economics, especially as Boeing has been able to make incremental range improvements, turning it into a true long haul aircraft.

    It has been revealed that at the same time, I can’t help but feel like it’s unusual how the airline has just seven A350s, with no more on order, and is now switching to the 787 for fleet renewal. Admittedly the A350 was ordered back in the day under a completely different management team, which also at one point thought the A380 was a good fit for the airline.

    So I am curious how the carrier’s fleet evolves. Will the seven A350s stick around, or will they eventually just be replaced by 787-10s? Even with airspace restrictions and headwinds, it seems like all of Malaysia Airlines’ routes should be within range for the 787-10, though admittedly London (LHR) might be on the cusp, depending on how airspace closures evolve, how dense of a configuration the airline selects, etc.

    The big challenge with the airline industry is that it’s never static, and decisions aren’t made in a vacuum. One management team makes one decision, and then a management team later on can’t just undo what the other management team did, without it being costly. So I get that they’re doing what they can….

    It has been revealed that malaysia Airlines is the newest customer for the Boeing 787, as the airline has ordered up to 16 787-10s, including 10 firm orders and six options. The airline intends to use this for a long haul expansion to Europe, as well as for flights in Asia-Pacific.

    It’s cool to see Malaysia Airlines continuing to grow, as the carrier has quite the order book at this point. I am curious if the airline keeps around the seven A350s in the long run, or how the airline manages its three wide body aircraft types.

    • The listed victim was Buffalo Biodiesel, which deals in used cooking oil, which it processes and sends to biodiesel refineries.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Thieves stole 350 gallons of cooking oil from an airport hotel in Pennsylvania. The haul was valued at $2,100, and the victim named by state police was a biofuel tech giant. Hotel kitchen grease has become valuable enough to steal. Used grease can fetch more than new! And it can eventually wind up fueling an airline flight and helping a carrier meet its environmental goals. Pennsylvania State Police responded on November 18 to the theft at 3400 Airport Road, the Days Hotel by Wyndham Allentown Airport / Lehigh Valley. The hotel has a restaurant and banquet facilities, so there’s a kitchen generating oil to collect. The loss works out to $6 per gallon. The listed victim was Buffalo Biodiesel, which deals in used cooking oil, which it processes and sends to biodiesel refineries. People steal astonishing things from hotels. I’ve covered mattresses, a lobby grand piano, and even a fireplace being taken. Two men carried an entire ATM out of a Country Inn & Suites. Used fryer oil seems much less attractive? But there’s a ready buyer for it, and hotels have been caught up in a much broader rash of cooking oil thefts: Hilton Short Hills, New Jersey: Police caught two men taking cooking oil around 3 a.m.. They’d arrived in a white Penske truck and were charged with theft and conspiracy. Brick Hotel, Pennsylvania: An attempted theft caused a used oil spill that required an environmental cleanup and closed a municipal parking lot. A hotel in Largs, Scotland: Two men arrived in a van around 1 a.m. and carried away cooking oil in blue buckets in order to convert it into biodiesel for profit. Old Ground Hotel, Ireland: Two men who pleaded guilty to stealing used cooking oil noted they wanted it to fuel their cars. In September, two defendants pleaded guilty in a federal case involving 19 people charged over a cooking oil theft operation spanning ten states. Trucks were taking the oil from restaurant collection tanks, warehouses consolidated it, the oil was sold across states and the effort was implicated in money laundering. The North American Renderers Association estimates annual used cooking oil theft at $300 million to $500 million. Once a hotel is done frying food, the oil can be collected and sold for processing into fuel. Buffalo Biodiesel supplies collection containers, picks up the oil, and processes it at its Tonawanda, New York facility before shipping it to refineries. These are the company’s processing tanks: Used cooking oil gets processed into sustainable aviation fuel. Refineries turn the fats and oils into fuel that can be blended with conventional jet fuel. Airlines want that fuel to meet environmental targets, and government subsidies prop up that market. This can create some very strange incentives. I’ve written about the arbitrage that makes used cooking oil more valuable than new oil in Malaysia. The government subsidizes cooking oil for food. Meanwhile, the biofuel market pays for oil classified as waste. In July 2025, subsidized fresh oil sold for 2.50 ringgit per kilogram while collectors could pay up to 3.50 ringgit for used oil. That’s a 40% spread. This turns into a greenwashing scam that actually creates more problems than it solves. By paying for “used” oil restaurants are encouraged to ‘create’ used oil, replacing their oil sooner. When you pay more than fresh oil costs, the incentive actually becomes skipping the cooking part altogether. But the environmental case depends on making use of waste that already exists. Instead, diverting fresh palm oil into that market increases the demand for new cooling oil production (and the pressure to clear land for it). The Simpsons got to this in 1998. In “Lard of the Dance,” Homer discovers that used grease has resale value: “Used grease is worth money?     • Less than two weeks after unanimously accepting CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation, Nvidia’s board has now, again unanimously, agreed to reinstate him.
    • According to recent reports, president Trump, no respecter of the division between boardroom and state, was heavily involved in Huang’s reinstallation.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Well, that was quick. Less than two weeks after unanimously accepting CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation, Nvidia’s board has now, again unanimously, agreed to reinstate him. This followed “a series of discussions and meetings . . . after which the board was satisfied with respect to Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.” The first hurdle must have been trickier than the second. Presumably even more importantly, based on “input” from “senior levels” of the U.S. government, the board was “confident” that Huang’s return posed “no national security risk.”.

    According to recent reports, president Trump, no respecter of the division between boardroom and state, was heavily involved in Huang’s reinstallation. In a post on Truth Social, he argued that it was needed “in order to ensure the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy.”.

    Recent findings suggest that on Monday, Nvidia’s stock jumped by over 30 percent, increasing its market cap by not far short of a trillion dollars. The tech-heavy NASDAQ rose nearly 6.5 percent, the S&P 500 by 4.75 percent. Trump views the stock market as a critical indicator of the nation’s economic health, not without reason, including the “wealth effect” created by rising stock prices. Booms can go bust, but, although calculating the effect of the AI build-out on the economy is not straightforward, by some estimates it may account for a quarter or more of current GDP growth.

    Trump also wrote that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Huang’s “return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” Trump added that Nvidia “should continue its thorough internal investigation of [its] compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and patriotic duty to protect U.S. national security.” And so it should.

    Various government agencies are investigating, as are a number of congressional committees. It was also unveiled on Monday that the U.S. is prohibiting the sale of AI chips to Megaspeed, the Singaporean data center firm previously connected to Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese agent with whom Nvidia’s CEO was in a relationship. The concern is that Megaspeed may have been diverting contraband chips to China. More generally, the administration has already tightened the rules governing exports of such chips to other countries where there is a diversion risk, a welcome, if overdue, step, as is the closing of the loophole that allowed enterprises in China and other hostile states to have remote access to the power of advanced American AI chips from businesses located in third countries.

    Recent findings suggest that this is a saga with a lot to unpack, much of which remains, at best, guesswork. Nevertheless, we do know (or can be pretty sure that) Nvidia’s board gave Jensen Huang considerable leeway when it came to the way he ran Nvidia, not least with regard to the way that so much of the organization’s decision-making was concentrated in him. That may well have underpinned Nvidia’s extraordinary success — a win for the U.S., as well as for Nvidia — but it also clearly played an important part in the current imbroglio and raises troubling questions about the consequences were Huang to step down again or, even if he weathers this crisis, at some later stage. It is mentioned that no man is irreplaceable, but that is not always so.

    Sources indicate that we also know that Nvidia, sometimes referred to as AI’s central bank, has played a key role in supporting the growth of earlier-stage companies. This has been criticized as a form of circular financing by Nvidia (the company is helping fund some of its client base), but it has played a vital part in the creation of an American AI ecosystem. Through Nvidia, Huang was a critical element in this ecosystem’s growth.

    And we know that the success of the American AI sector has geopolitical as well as commercial implications. There is an AI race between China and the U.S. The U.S. must hang on to the lead it has built up — here’s the catch — in no small part with Nvidia’s assistance. Huang has argued against overly broad U.S. restrictions on the export of U.S. chips, arguing that they will only encourage China to make their own, an unconvincing argument given the importance Beijing puts on autarky. Of course, Nvidia would benefit financially (for a while) by selling AI chips to China, but it is not in our strategic interest to allow it.

    Huang is entitled to his views, but they do not entitle his manufacturer to evade U.S, export controls or even to turn a blind eye should Nvidia’s customers “divert” chips to forbidden destinations. The question of whether this occurred will almost certainly be the main focus of the investigations. It is a question that dwarfs (however much corporate governance purists may object) Huang’s reckless choice of companionship and, in this respect, his lack of candor with Nvidia’s board. The investigations will lead where they will lead. They will also be highly politicized. Regardless of the investigations’ conclusions, they will be a major distraction and, as such, unhelpful to Nvidia and the U.S. AI sector more broadly. That will be a win that should never have been handed to Beijing.

    The Editors comprise the senior editorial staff of National Review magazine and nationalreview.com.

    It has been revealed that with the number of close calls we see at airports nowadays, it’s great to see when pilots or air traffic controllers go above and beyond to be observant, and exhibit good situational awareness. So along those lines, here’s a case of a pilot paying close attention to ensure everyone’s safety, and then an air traffic controller being frustrated by that….

    YouTube channel You can see ATC has the air traffic control audio and a visualization of an interaction that happened shortly before noon on November 21, 2026, at San Francisco International Airport (SFO).

    In this interaction, a SkyWest Embraer E175 operating on behalf of American Eagle had just landed on runway 28L, after flying from Los Angeles (LAX). The pilots were switched to the ground frequency, and that’s when things swiftly went downhill:.

    The SkyWest pilots then continued their taxi, and when they got to the gate, the conversation continued:.

    When you screw up, I suppose it’s human nature to get a bit defensive, and I think that’s exactly what happened here.

    Sources indicate that credit to the SkyWest pilots for their situational awareness here. They were instructed to taxi in front of another plane, and another plane was instructed to give way to them, but never read back those instructions. The air traffic controller absolutely should have caught that, and as a pilot, they 100% did the correct thing by noticing the lack of a read back, and erring on the side of caution.

    This isn’t just some theoretical risk, but ground collisions are the most common kinds of accidents involving commercial aircraft. Could the SkyWest pilots have mentioned “we’re holding short because the other plane didn’t read back instructions?” Sure, but it seems like the time gap here was a matter of seconds, and they didn’t want to step on the radio calls of another pilot, in case they were going to read back.

    What I think is really unprofessional is how the air traffic controller then responded to this:.

    Recent findings suggest that the pilots of a SkyWest flight decided to hold short of a taxiway after they observed the plane that was supposed to give way to them not reading back the correct instructions. That was absolutely the right move, and the air traffic controller should’ve caught that.

    Recent findings suggest that when the pilots explained why they held short, the air traffic controller didn’t respond particularly well. Then when they asked for a phone number, she noted the pilots would be talking to someone else, and she clearly wasn’t having it. But then she was also mad when the pilot explained very briefly what was going on, saying the conversation should happen off frequency… a conversation she wasn’t willing to have!

    This is a clear situation where you have two very professional pilots, and one very unprofessional air traffic controller.

    What do you make of this SFO ATC interaction?

    According to recent reports, russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday. (Win McNamee/AFP via Getty Images).

    That was the greeting, complete with a lengthy handshake, President Donald Trump gave Vladimir Putin before two high-level meetings Thursday, including the first “trilateral” session with sitting U.S., Russian and Chinese heads of state.

    “It’s nice to see you,” Trump told Putin before a private one-on-one meeting in China’s Shenzhen economic zone, before pulling the Russian strongman close and saying something into his ear too low for journalists’ microphones to pick up.

    In a recent development, trump and Putin then posed for the cameras with wide grins, again underscoring the U.S. president’s closeness with a world leader who has been partially shunned by the West since he launched a war with Ukraine in February 2022. Trump on Thursday also appeared several times alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping, who like Putin has been scorned by Republican and Democratic lawmakers for years.

    Industry observers note that “We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We've known each other for a long time. And I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this — or, at least, start,” Trump told reporters as Putin beamed from a few feet away.

    They later were joined by Xi for a group photo before sitting down at a round wooden table with a large arrangement of pink flowers in the center.

    In a recent development, his interactions with and comments about Putin and Xi reflect Trump’s belief that his personal relationships can bend them toward U.S. interests. But that gambit clashed Thursday with his second term’s expiration date — the White House did not disclose any agreements reached during his various meetings with the two leaders, nor did Trump hold a press conference following the three-way session.

    Both Putin and Xi are adept at playing the geopolitical long game. The 26 months left in Trump’s term is a relatively short amount of time compared to the duo that has been in power for a combined 56 years and will remain in place for the foreseeable future.

    Indeed, even Trump acknowledged the first-ever meeting might not immediately yield much progress on its ostensible goal: paring each powers’ nuclear weapons arsenals.

    “I must say, it's, quite frankly, a very hard thing to do, because once you have the nuclear weapons, it's very hard to not have them. It's very hard to give them up as the leader of a country,” Trump stated as Putin and Xi looked on. “Something that's very difficult to say, because … it's the way life works.

    Recent findings suggest that “You know, you have thousands of weapons and you're supposed to give them up, and yet you have countries in addition to us, in much smaller numbers, but they have nuclear weapons, also,” he added. “So it's not an easy thing to do and give them up.”.

    Trump, who was convicted by a Upcoming York jury in a business records case and who saw a federal election interference case against him dismissed only because of his reelection, also appeared to join Putin’s resistance to international criminal justice entities that have alleged Putin has committed war crimes in Ukraine.

    “In another area of potential cooperation between us, I'll be suggesting ways to protect our nations’ sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court, which has gotten out of control, which I believe we all agree has really strayed far from beyond its jurisdiction,” Trump said, a statement that would be almost unthinkable to hear from any other sitting U.S. president.

    In a recent development, other world leaders, including democratically elected ones, at two Pacific region economic summits in which Trump participated this week did not receive the kind of cordial and personal treatment from the U.S. side that Putin and Xi enjoyed.

    “This summit was nothing but a glorified photo op and a gift to Putin and Xi,” Schumer said.

    In a recent development, sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., an Armed Services Committee member, wanted Trump to press Putin over Ukraine.

    “Ukraine is defending itself from Putin's aggression, which this president should be opposing as well,” Blumenthal mentioned Tuesday. “We are spending no money on Ukraine. Let's be very clear: Arms to Ukraine are purchased by Ukraine with financial support from Europe, not America. … Let's support Ukraine.”.

    Recent findings suggest that on spending, Trump and administration officials have been pressing Senate Republicans to quickly pass another budget reconciliation measure with $350 billion more for the Defense Department. However, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and other GOP senators have signaled in the last 24 hours that they had shelved the notion of another fast-track spending measure.

    According to recent reports, “You have to have a path forward. You've got to get on it, and you have to protect it, and that takes 50 in the Senate,” Thune told reporters Thursday. “And then you've got to get it through the House. As you probably saw yesterday, a lot of folks in the House were lobbing grenades at the Senate reconciliation bill and complaints about it not being offset, et cetera.     💡 Key Takeaways

    • Economy class meals can seem like quite the downgrade should one be accustomed to the elevated fare at the pointy end of the plane.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I’ve flown back and forth across the Atlantic dozens of times in all cabins, including many times in economy. JetBlue definitely stands out as being my favorite, and dare I say it, the most premium of all the transatlantic economy flights I’ve experienced.

    My most recent trip was from Europe to Boston (BOS) for the opening of JetBlue’s newest BlueHouse location. The airline covered my flights for the event, but had no input in this article. I’d like to share some of the reasons that JetBlue’s transatlantic experience impressed me so much.

    Economy class meals can seem like quite the downgrade should one be accustomed to the elevated fare at the pointy end of the plane.

    JetBlue presently partners with NYC-based Dig Inn for its transatlantic economy-class meals, and they’re far better than average. They also offer products from a range of interesting brands, rather than just your classic soda labels.

    Here’s an example of the drinks menu on my flight from Amsterdam to Boston.

    Meals are served in these stylish, reusable, matte-black sealed containers. I’d love to see more airlines do more to reduce their waste like this.

    I was very happy with my choice of chicken pesto pasta salad as the main course, accompanied by sides of beet and carrot slaw and snap peas with feta. The fresh, flavorful, yet cold dishes were far better than many of the reheated slop I’ve been served in economy before.

    It has been revealed that I was equally impressed by the breakfast I had on the morning departure back from Boston to London Heathrow (LHR). I went for the Bubly sparkling water again, as I avoid coffee on a plane unless it’s served as espresso. The stuff they pour out of those vats is pretty much just glorified dirty water.

    As far as pre-landing light meals go, this pizza thing was pretty good, too.

    In addition to the main meal and pre-landing light bite, JetBlue keeps a well-stocked pantry at the back of the Airbus A321LR.

    JetBlue has been offering fast, free, in-flight Wi-Fi for as long as I can remember. The same cannot be mentioned for some full-service carriers, which still can’t guarantee a reliable, fast, and free connection on their transatlantic flights.

    According to recent reports, they’ve also added some fun tech features, like the ability to choose the elements for the main meal service via the IFE screen, even in economy. I think it has a more premium feel than being asked “chicken or beef?”.

    I’m not a frequent JetBlue flyer, so I couldn’t really make the most of the fun personalization features, such as the option to continue watching the movie where you left off on your last flight.

    According to recent reports, being given anything more than the standard pillow and blanket in economy is a rare bonus. It had been so long since my last JetBlue flight in economy that I’d forgotten about the complimentary Snooze Kit.

    I prefer to use my AirPods to earplugs, but I did make good use of the eye mask for a mid-flight nap.

    I’ve flown over my fair share of narrow bodies on long-haul flights, and I genuinely don’t know why such a fuss is made about them being terrible.

    JetBlue’s version of the aircraft has comfy seats, with standard Core (economy) seats having 32 inches of pitch. Another common complaint I hear is that there are fewer toilets. For a plane with far fewer passengers (only 114 in economy), fewer toilets kind of makes sense. I didn’t once find myself waiting in line to use the bathroom on either flight.

    Recent findings suggest that for what it’s worth, there are two lavatories for 114 economy passengers, so that’s one lavatory per 57 passengers. That’s a little lower than the industry standard, but not by much. For example, American’s standard 787-9s have five lavatories for 255 economy seats, so that’s a ratio of one lavatory per 51 passengers.

    According to recent reports, if you’ve only got the budget or the points for economy for your next trip to Europe, I couldn’t recommend JetBlue more. They now fly to eight cities in Europe, the planes are comfortable and modern, and the in-flight food and beverage is top of the game for economy.
